REA itself offers both CLI and MCP interfaces, so this benchmark does not establish that LeanREA replaces all REA workflows.

The pinned project declares MIT for its skill and benchmark code and credits REA’s code and documentation for many workflow details; it explicitly disclaims affiliation. External analysis tools, model services and target applications retain separate requirements and terms. The benchmark document is dated 2026-10-16; the initial public commit is dated 2026-10-17, and only the README changed before the reviewed pin. This collection inspected source and recomputed published metric totals without running the skill, models, tools or targets.

name: UU Remote on Linux: an unofficial protocol implementation
description_en: Implements an unofficial native Linux host for NetEase UU Remote, using protocol behavior the maintainer says was recovered from official-client traffic and shipped programs. The Rust implementation connects selected desktop, input and auxiliary-tool channels to Linux services; an additional Linux viewer remains experimental. The author attributes development to Claude and Codex, without establishing REA use.
description_zh: 实现网易 UU 远程的非官方原生 Linux 被控端；维护者称协议行为来自对官方客户端流量及已发布程序的调查。Rust 实现将选定的桌面、输入和辅助工具通道连接到 Linux 服务，另有仍处于实验阶段的 Linux 控制端。作者将开发归因于 Claude 与 Codex，未确立 REA 使用。
requirements: Reviewed version 0.2.8 implements selected protocol formats and session behavior in native Rust with small C components, without Wine or bundled NetEase binaries. The additional Linux viewer is experimental. Cargo.toml declares GPL-3.0-or-later; dependencies and official clients/services retain separate terms. This is not recovered vendor source or a replacement cloud backend.

The host needs Linux, stable Rust, a C toolchain, pkg-config, X11 development libraries and FFmpeg. GTK3 supports graphical login; the optional viewer also needs SDL2. Wayland/portal builds require additional libraries and authorized desktop access. Dependencies vary by feature; arbitrary Linux compatibility is not established.

UU cloud services remain required; the host and experimental viewer interoperate with supported official clients and hosts. Account connections use the user’s own authorized account; experimental remote assistance requires an explicitly enabled host and recipient-provided connection details. The project is unaffiliated with NetEase, and no security audit or complete protocol equivalence is established.

Public parsing and initialization code has synthetic checks for malformed inputs, capability replies and echo correlation. Local/virtual WebRTC peers test pending-desktop responses, independent tool connections and session isolation. These are implementation checks, not an independent official-client conformance corpus. This entry is source-reviewed; tests and device behavior were not independently run.

The README reports real-machine GNOME/X11 use and selected GNOME Wayland checks; other desktop coverage is largely virtual-machine based. Its viewer acceptance matrix is explicitly partial, with different official-host coverage for clipboard, audio, codecs and keyboards. These remain author-reported observations, not generally applicable compatibility results.

Wayland remains experimental, with single-screen and resolution/recovery limits. Multi-monitor switching is under development; HDR, privacy-screen mode, microphone forwarding and the Linux pre-login screen are unsupported. Restrictive-network relay behavior is not thoroughly tested. Cloud behavior and supported versions may change independently of this snapshot.

name: Perfect Dark: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs Perfect Dark’s Nintendo 64 code with a documented matching-ROM build. The project combines reconstructed source with assets from a user-supplied original ROM, then checks version-specific artifact hashes. It is a reproducible-build research case, distinct from the separate native PC port; matching results remain project-reported here.
description_zh: 重建 Perfect Dark 的 Nintendo 64 代码，并提供生成一致 ROM 的构建流程。项目将重建源码与使用者自备原 ROM 中的素材结合，再检查各版本产物的哈希。这是可复现构建研究案例，与独立的原生 PC 移植不同；此处的一致性结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: The reviewed GitHub repository mirrors Ryan Dwyer’s GitLab project. README describes a complete matching decompilation; six build targets cover NTSC beta, NTSC 1.0/final, PAL beta/final and Japanese final, with ntsc-final as default. This reconstructs an N64 ROM, not a Windows/Linux/macOS game executable or the separate Perfect Dark PC port.

Supply an independently authorized original ROM in non-byteswapped .z64 form, with header 0x80371240, named for the selected ROMID. make extract reads assets and comparison segments from that ROM; final builds also reuse extracted boot code. Existing extracted files are not overwritten, so modified inputs can invalidate matching results.

The documented host setup is Linux: GNU Make, host C/C++ tools, Python 3, MIPS binutils/GCC, armips, Capstone development files and the listed 32-bit libc headers. Initialize the pinned ido-static-recomp submodule. Matching mode reconstructs IDO 5.3 and 7.1 compiler tools from its IRIX inputs; optional GCC builds are nonmatching and limited to ntsc-1.0/ntsc-final.

After building, make test runs quiet MD5 verification against the selected version’s checksum manifest, including the final ROM and intermediate artifacts. The README also documents comparing base/built ROM hashes. These check output identity for the supplied version, not gameplay-path coverage or performance. The mutable status page reports all six versions complete/matching; this collection did not rerun those checks.

The repository declares MIT for source; original ROMs and extracted game assets retain separate rights. Compiler components have their own terms, including the submodule’s SGI notice for IDO 5.3; the project’s MIT declaration does not replace them. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: TCLimate: reconstructing selected TCL Home cloud controls
description_en: Implements selected TCL Home air-conditioner controls and electricity reporting in a native macOS menu-bar app. It adapts earlier community protocol work and documents an Android-module investigation to recover a separate statistics request. Reported validation checks cloud state, not independent physical operation or complete device equivalence.
description_zh: 在原生 macOS 菜单栏应用中实现选定的 TCL Home 空调控制与用电量报告。项目改编既有社区协议实现，并记录通过调查 Android 模块恢复另一条统计请求的过程。报告的验证检查云端状态，不等于独立核实设备实际运行或完整设备等价性。
requirements: Reviewed v0.1.6 beta requires macOS 14+, internet access and a TCL account with already-paired ACs. Building needs Swift 6.0+, Xcode Command Line Tools and a persistent signing certificate for the packaged app. Pairing still uses TCL Home; local LAN control and direct Google sign-in are absent.

The protocol implementation credits nemesa’s MIT-licensed Home Assistant integration. The electricity API was reportedly identified through Android Flutter-module inspection and a successful request capture; original packages, captures and detailed investigation logs are not included in the repository. The inspected repository does not establish the collection report’s REA/mitmproxy attribution.

Source guards commands using reported model/state fields, restricts target temperature to whole degrees from 16–30°C, and checks reported state after sending. Optimistic UI changes are not themselves confirmation; unsuccessful confirmation is marked. Extra controls depend on available fields and modes, rather than assuming every AC supports them.

Author validation covers a Pakistan account and two Split AC-1 units: authentication, discovery, reported state, power, temperature and daily electricity. Modes, fan, airflow and other optional controls lack physical validation; other regions/models remain unverified. Cloud confirmation does not independently establish airflow or compressor operation.

Energy parsing preserves genuine zeros, excludes invalid readings and leaves missing days as gaps; a seven-day total requires all seven readings. No persistent energy history or cost estimate is implemented. Offline tests are reported but absent from the reviewed tree/package targets. This source review did not run tests or devices.

MIT covers project code, with attribution retained for the earlier integration. Official services and third-party material retain separate terms. This is an unofficial cloud-dependent client, not recovered TCL source or firmware; APIs may change independently of the app.

name: Universal Modder
description_en: Packages agent skills, three role briefs, a Python CLI and preconfigured fal MCP settings for modding PC games the user owns. Its reverse-engineering guidance sends managed, native and data-format work to external decompilers and debuggers, and requires a round-trip check before a reverse-engineered file format is used; one worked example ships an Age of Empires II sprite writer built this way. It is a modding toolkit with agent-written field notes, not a game decompilation, and its example results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 为修改用户自有的 PC 游戏打包智能体技能、三份角色说明、Python 命令行工具及预配置的 fal MCP 设置。其逆向分析指南把托管代码、原生代码和数据格式工作交给外部反编译器与调试器，并要求逆向得到的文件格式先通过往返检查再投入使用；其中一个示例附带按此方法实现的 Age of Empires II 精灵写入器。它是附带智能体实践笔记的模组工具包，不是游戏反编译重建，示例结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: The reviewed pin is Python package version 0.2.0. It ships twelve Agent Skills-format skills, three subagent role files, the um CLI and per-client settings for the hosted fal MCP server, with install routes for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code/Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode. The host needs Git, Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg, with uv recommended and Blender only for 3D-to-sprite rendering; Windows capture, input and launch commands run natively or from WSL.

Work starts from a game installation the user owns. The toolkit supplies no game files, ROMs or decompiled code, and tells agents to keep decompiles and extracted assets outside the repository. Asset generation needs a fal API key or fal’s browser sign-in; a local ComfyUI server is an image alternative, and Sprixen is a separate paid API. Decompilers, debuggers, loaders and MCP servers named in the skills, such as ILSpy, Cpp2IL, Ghidra, IDA, Cheat Engine, Frida and RenderDoc, are installed separately.

The reverse-engineering skill asks agents to read decompiled code, data or live memory, confirm guesses dynamically, and prove a reverse-engineered file format with a decode–encode–decode round trip before writing new files. It reports that the Age of Empires II DE .sld writer was accepted at 0.9/255 mean error on a stock sprite, and that a ported Terraria boss-movement rule matched recorded velocities at 99.9%. The AoE2 example reports in-game testing in September 2026; these are author results, not reproduced here.

Repository CI runs the Python tests, every CLI help screen, a knowledge-base index check and a publish lint that blocks game files, decompiled code and secrets. These checks cover the toolkit, not whether a mod works in a particular game. Knowledge-base field notes are agent-written and PR-reviewed with self-declared status and verification sections; they are not independently verified compatibility records. This collection reviewed source and documentation without running the CLI, skills, games or examples.

Project rules limit work to games the user owns, offline or on servers the user hosts, and refuse injection into anti-cheat-protected online clients, cheats against other players, and DRM, anti-cheat or ownership-check bypasses. The repository declares MIT for its code and bundles fonts under the SIL OFL; generated assets follow fal and model terms, and games, loaders and external tools keep their own terms. Its safety notes cite takedowns of projects that shipped no assets. The reviewed sources establish no REA connection.

name: Browserbase plugin: re-hosting Claude in Chrome’s browser bridge
description_en: Stands in for the Claude in Chrome extension side of Claude Code’s local browser bridge and runs the requested actions in Browserbase cloud browsers. The author’s thread describes the reverse-engineered framing, a 4-byte little-endian length before each JSON tool call, and the plugin maps 17 named tools onto Stagehand/CDP operations. It is an archived interoperability shim with several placeholder tools, not recovered Anthropic code or a verified equivalent of the extension.
description_zh: 在 Claude Code 本地浏览器桥接中替代 Claude in Chrome 扩展一端，把请求的操作交给 Browserbase 云端浏览器执行。作者的帖子串描述了逆向得到的消息格式，即每条 JSON 工具调用前加 4 字节小端长度；插件则将 17 个具名工具映射为 Stagehand／CDP 操作。这是已归档的互操作适配层，部分工具仅为占位实现，并非恢复出的 Anthropic 代码，也未经验证与扩展等价。
requirements: The reviewed main branch is archived, and its commits are dated 2025-12-27. A SessionStart hook launches a Node forwarding server that moves any existing claude-mcp-browser-bridge-<user> socket in the temporary directory aside and listens in its place. Messages carry a 4-byte little-endian length plus JSON; only the execute_tool method is accepted, with 17 named tool handlers and errors for anything else.

Requires Claude Code with plugin support, the Claude in Chrome extension, Node.js 18+, the Browserbase SDK and Stagehand npm packages, and a Browserbase API key and project ID. As written, the start hook looks for the extension only under the macOS Chrome profile directory and stops when it is missing, so other hosts fail that check.

Navigation, input, screenshots, page reading, form filling and JavaScript run through Stagehand on cloud sessions; console and network reads rely on the plugin’s own listeners and page-injected tracking. update_plan only echoes the submitted plan, shortcuts return an empty list or a placeholder, and image upload and GIF export are placeholders. The author’s thread counts 19 extension tools; the reviewed dispatcher names 17.

The protocol account comes from the author’s X thread, not Anthropic documentation, and no captures or comparisons against the real extension are published. package.json declares Node test scripts, but the reviewed tree has no tests directory. This collection did not run the plugin, a cloud session or the extension; the undocumented local interface may change with Claude Code or extension updates.

README states MIT, but the reviewed tree has no LICENSE file and GitHub detects no license. Claude Code, the Claude in Chrome extension and Browserbase services keep their own terms, and browsed pages are processed on Browserbase infrastructure. The reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: Visor: an independent Ray-Ban Meta glasses client
description_en: Implements an Android replacement for the Meta AI companion app that speaks the Ray-Ban Meta glasses’ own Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct protocol, imports media, exposes settings and answers “Hey Meta” with a model the user chooses. The project wiki documents the link layers, encryption, services and Meta-side ownership steps, and lists 153 open questions. Testing is on real glasses rather than test suites, so behavior beyond the stated model and firmware remains unverified.
description_zh: 实现可替代 Meta AI 配套应用的 Android 客户端：直接使用 Ray-Ban Meta 眼镜自有的蓝牙与 Wi-Fi Direct 协议，导入媒体、提供设置，并用用户选择的模型回应“Hey Meta”。项目 wiki 记录了链路分层、加密、服务及 Meta 端的所有权流程，并列出 153 个未解问题。项目以实机试用代替测试套件，因此所述型号和固件之外的行为仍未经验证。
requirements: Reviewed just after release v1.3.1 (2026-10-18). README targets Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) tested on firmware 72387580077200100; other Meta glasses are untested. It needs an Android 10+ phone, a Meta account using password or email-code login (passkeys do not work) and, for the assistant, an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible API key. The glasses accept one session at a time, so Visor and the Meta AI app displace each other.

Setup makes Visor the glasses’ owner app through Meta’s login and ownership-receipt services, so it still depends on a Meta account and Meta servers for setup, frame style and language packs. Source builds need three client tokens from the official Meta AI app, which the repository does not include; without them the app builds but login and ownership fail. Release builds read them from CI secrets.

Building needs JDK 21 and the Android SDK with platform 37. CI builds a debug APK with Gradle, and tagged releases publish a signed APK with a SHA-256 file; README lists the release certificate fingerprint. Modules separate wire format and ciphers, transport, session, identity, media, settings and the assistant, which stands in for Meta’s server with Claude or an OpenAI-compatible model.

There are no test suites: CONTRIBUTING asks for hardware trials and wire.log excerpts for protocol changes, and CLAUDE.md says the app works on real glasses as of 2026-10-05. The wiki marks unconfirmed facts and lists open questions, including unread payloads and model-specific values; CLAUDE.md also refers to a desktop Python client snapshot that the repository does not contain. This collection read source and documentation without running the app or glasses.

Visor is AGPL-3.0 and states it is unaffiliated with Meta or EssilorLuxottica; Meta’s services, app tokens, firmware and trademarks keep their own terms. CONTRIBUTING forbids getting unsigned software past the glasses’ signature checks. Claude is one selectable assistant backend, the repository’s CLAUDE.md is a contributor guide, and the reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: Super Mario Sunshine: a native PC port from an AI-assisted decompilation
description_en: Builds a native PC port of Super Mario Sunshine’s North American release from a pinned matching-decompilation fork, adding a host platform layer for graphics, disc, audio, input and OS services. The fork’s README says AI was used extensively to reconstruct and match its code; the port documents scripted regression hashes and lockstep comparisons with retail captures. Functions that do not yet match can still behave differently from retail, and the game must come from the user’s own disc image.
description_zh: 以固定版本的一致性反编译分支为基础，构建 Super Mario Sunshine 北美版的原生 PC 移植，并为图形、光盘、音频、输入和系统服务提供宿主平台层。该分支的 README 称，其代码的重建与匹配大量借助 AI；移植项目记录了脚本化回归哈希，以及与原版捕获数据的逐步对照。尚未匹配的函数仍可能与原版行为不同，游戏数据须来自使用者自己的光盘镜像。
requirements: Targets only the North American GMSE01 Rev 0 release. README reports the 32-bit Linux and macOS builds as playable, 64-bit Linux as playable but still being tested stage by stage, and 64-bit Windows as booting under Wine with native runtime checks. macOS builds x86_64, run under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon, because native arm64 cannot map game memory below 4 GiB.

Requires the user’s own GMSE01 Rev 0 disc image as .iso, .gcm or Dolphin .ciso; the port reads models, textures, levels, music and movies from it at run time and ships no game data. Given the image, the build also makes a standalone executable containing the game’s files, which README says must not be shared. Optional language, texture and HD-cutscene packs are separate.

build.sh and run.sh drive CMake, Python 3, patch, SDL2 and a host compiler: Ubuntu/Debian multilib GCC for the default 32-bit Linux build, Homebrew LLVM clang targeting x86_64 on macOS, or MSYS2 MINGW64 GCC on Windows. The decomp submodule is pinned to sms-english 967436b; PC-only changes are patches applied to copies of its sources, and the separate decomp build to a matching mario.dol uses its own GameCube toolchain.

At that pin, the fork’s PROGRESS.md reports, as of 2026-09-27, 99.57% fuzzy, 72.94% byte-perfect and 33.18% source-linked code, with 12,002 of 12,904 functions matching and a byte-identical rebuilt DOL that still links extracted objects for unfinished code; its README gives slightly higher 2026-09-29 figures. The port compiles the decomp’s 588 game, JSystem and THPPlayer units, so non-matching functions can still diverge from retail. It reports scripted headless runs hashed against a baseline and compared between 32- and 64-bit builds, lockstep tracing against retail Dolphin captures and qemu-ppc checks of math routines; this collection ran none of them.

The port is MIT-licensed (SoftwareAura LLC) and the decomp fork is CC0-1.0; the game and the user’s disc contents keep separate rights. AI involvement is stated by the fork’s README and agent guides, which describe Claude and Codex orchestrators, without measuring it; the reported X post adds no separate technical evidence. REA use is not established.

name: Majora’s Mask: matching US N64 decompilation
description_en: Recreates a C source base for The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask from information in the game and static or dynamic analysis, then rebuilds the US Nintendo 64 ROM. The build takes assets and assembly from a user-supplied ROM and checks the output against stored MD5 checksums. The team states it will not produce a PC port; the separately curated Zelda 64: Recompiled only credits it for headers and some functions.
description_zh: 依据游戏内信息和静态或动态分析，为《塞尔达传说：姆吉拉的假面》重建 C 源码库，并重新构建美版 Nintendo 64 ROM。构建流程从使用者自备的 ROM 中取得素材和汇编，再用仓库保存的 MD5 校验输出。团队声明不会制作 PC 移植；另行收录的 Zelda 64: Recompiled 只注明借用了其头文件和部分函数。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress decompilation whose codebase may still change drastically, and warns that some parts of the ROM may not yet be shiftable, so modifications can be difficult. Only N64 US 1.0 is supported; the Makefile also lists a WIP N64 Japan 1.1 target with checksum comparison disabled. Majora’s Mask 3D is out of scope, and the output is an N64 ROM, not a PC executable.

Supply your own US Majora’s Mask ROM as the base ROM; .z64, .n64 and .v64 byte orders are accepted. The repository includes no game assets or assembly: the build decompresses the supplied ROM and derives files, assets and disassembled code and data from it before compiling a ROM and a compressed ROM.

The documented host is Linux, native or under WSL or a VM, with Debian or Ubuntu recommended: Git, build-essential, MIPS binutils, curl, Python 3 with pip and venv, libpng and libxml2. macOS and Docker have separate guides. The default compiler is a static recompilation of IDO 5.3 and 7.1 that the tools Makefile downloads from decompals/ido-static-recomp; GCC and NON_MATCHING builds turn the checksum comparison off.

A default build checks both ROMs against stored MD5 values and prints OK or FAILED; FAILED means a bad base ROM or non-matching code. CI builds the US version in matching mode and Japan 1.1 as non-matching, using base ROMs from the project’s build container. The project’s mutable progress badge read 100% at review while the README still says WIP; this collection did not rerun the build.

The reviewed tree has no top-level license file and GitHub detects no license, so source reuse terms are unstated; ROM contents and derived assets keep their own rights. The README forbids contributions from anyone who has ever accessed leaked Nintendo 64 SDK, libultra or Zelda 64 source. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: wine-uwp: running packaged Windows Store apps on a patched Wine
description_en: Extends Wine 11.17 so that signed MSIX Store apps, with Shapr3D as the main target, install and run on Linux without their source or symbols. About 49,000 changed lines add a DirectComposition implementation, composition swap chains and an app-model host, while Microsoft’s own XAML and app-model DLLs, harvested from a Windows 11 image on the user’s machine, run unmodified. The author says Claude did most of the reverse engineering and code; app support is uneven and checked by a project regression suite.
description_zh: 扩展 Wine 11.17，使已签名的 MSIX 商店应用（主要目标为 Shapr3D）无需源码或符号即可在 Linux 上安装运行。约 49,000 行改动新增了 DirectComposition 实现、合成交换链和应用模型宿主；微软自己的 XAML 与应用模型 DLL 则在使用者机器上从 Windows 11 镜像中提取后原样运行。作者称大部分逆向工程和代码由 Claude 完成；各应用支持程度不一，由项目回归测试检查。
requirements: README’s app table reports Shapr3D sketching, modelling, menus, cloud sync, sign-in and STL/PDF export; Solitaire playable; Media Player playing audio from its own UI; Calculator fully working; Feedback Hub interactive; and Camera only reaching its own error page. Shapr3D for Linux (58d9173) packages this same pinned wine-uwp commit as a beta AppImage and Flatpak; it is unofficial and not affiliated with Shapr3D.

Needs the user’s own app package (.msix or .msixbundle, or Shapr3D’s .appinstaller, from which setup downloads about 1.8 GB) and Windows components extracted from Microsoft’s free Windows 11 evaluation ISO or another Windows 11 image. Neither the repositories nor the release packages contain them, and a commit hook refuses Windows binaries. Shapr3D also needs an account and a browser sign-in.

Building copies the vendored wine/ files over the Wine 11.17 source, then runs autoreconf, configure with --enable-archs=x86_64 and make; the WinRT stand-in shims build with clang-cl and lld-link against Windows SDK headers fetched by xwin. Shapr3D for Linux needs 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.38+, working Vulkan drivers and about 11 GB free during setup, and its releases build with flatpak-builder on the freedesktop 25.08 SDK.

regress.sh requires Calculator to stay pixel-identical to a committed baseline and other apps to come up on a private Xvfb display; release.sh smoke-tests that an empty setup reaches Shapr3D’s first screen. The Findings logs record failed approaches as well as fixes. These checks are project-reported; this collection did not build Wine or run any app.

Neither repository has a top-level license file, and GitHub detects none. The vendored Wine files carry LGPL-2.1-or-later headers and the setup app’s Cargo manifest declares the same; the shims and investigation tools state no license. Harvested Microsoft components and Store apps keep their own terms, and the plan notes that a distributable product would need clean-room replacements for them. The author’s X posts disclose heavy Claude assistance; REA use is not established.

name: DLSSNR-AMD: reimplementing DLSS 5 neural rendering for RDNA4
description_en: Reimplements the neural-rendering network of NVIDIA’s DLSS 5 library as Vulkan compute shaders for AMD RX 9000 (RDNA4) cards and supplies it to games through an NGX-compatible core and ReShade or Vulkan-layer routes. The weights are not distributed: installers extract them, hash-checked, from the user’s own nvngx_dlssnr.dll 310.9.16 or 310.8.0. The project compares its output with NVIDIA’s DLL on an RTX 5090 and reports close, not bit-identical, pictures.
description_zh: 将 NVIDIA DLSS 5 库中的神经渲染网络重新实现为面向 AMD RX 9000（RDNA4）显卡的 Vulkan 计算着色器，并通过兼容 NGX 的核心模块以及 ReShade 或 Vulkan 层等途径提供给游戏。项目不分发权重：安装程序从使用者自己的 nvngx_dlssnr.dll 310.9.16 或 310.8.0 中提取权重并核对哈希。项目将输出与 NVIDIA DLL 在 RTX 5090 上的结果对比，报告画面接近但并非逐位一致。
requirements: The reviewed 0.0.x main targets RX 9000 cards because the network needs RDNA4 FP8 matrix instructions, reached through VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix; README says it was tested only on an RX 9070 XT. Linux under Steam/Proton with Mesa 26.2+ is the main version; Windows is an experimental preview tested with AMD Software 26.9.2, slower by default and closer to Linux with precompiled ACO machine code. OpenGL games are unsupported, and README warns against online games with anti-cheat.

Requires the user’s own nvngx_dlssnr.dll, version 310.9.16 (both models) or 310.8.0 (the old model only); other versions are refused, and a model file is written only when every extracted entry matches a known hash. README says packages containing the model must not be shared. The optional int4-mixed network derives its weights at install from the user’s model and project calibration tables, which THIRD_PARTY.md says hold no weight values.

The documented build runs on Ubuntu 24.04 with git, curl, Python 3, CMake, Ninja, MinGW-w64 and multilib g++; fetch_deps.sh pins third-party components, including glslang 16.5.0 for reproducible SPIR-V, and the Windows DLLs are cross-compiled. Games reach the network through an NGX core loaded by OptiScaler-NR, for DirectX 11/12 titles with an upscaler option, or through ReShade-based routes that estimate motion from the picture.

For the 310.9.16 model, the verification notes report single-frame PSNR of 49.15–50.59 dB and SSIM of about 0.997 against NVIDIA’s unmodified DLL on an RTX 5090, plus short moving sequences, from one Tomb Raider (2013) frame and its downscales; the 310.8.0 comparison reports 45.56–49.06 dB. These are project measurements on one AMD card; this collection ran neither side.

MIT covers the repository’s code; third-party components keep their own licenses, including GPL-3.0 OptiScaler-NR shipped as released. NVIDIA’s DLL and weights remain NVIDIA’s, and the project states it is not affiliated with NVIDIA or AMD. The repository does not describe how the network structure was recovered; its CLAUDE.md addresses coding assistants but does not establish AI authorship. REA use is not established.

name: Breath of the Wild: per-function matching decompilation of the Switch executable
description_en: Reimplements part of Breath of the Wild’s Switch v1.5.0 main executable in C++ and checks each function against the original machine code. The project calls itself a hybrid decompilation/reimplementation: it contains no assets, its ELF holds only reimplemented functions and cannot run the game, and porting is an explicit non-goal.
description_zh: 以 C++ 重新实现《塞尔达传说 旷野之息》Switch v1.5.0 主程序的部分代码，并逐个函数与原始机器码比对。项目自称是反编译与重新实现的混合体：不含游戏素材，生成的 ELF 仅包含已重新实现的函数、无法运行游戏，移植到其他平台也明确不是目标。
requirements: README calls this an experimental work-in-progress decompilation of Switch v1.5.0. The About page scopes it to the main executable (game code and most statically linked libraries), excluding RomFS assets, dynamically linked SDK libraries, libcurl, NEX and most of Havok. Functions are matched individually rather than placed at original addresses, so this is not a whole-executable matching build, a playable game or a port.

Setup needs the user’s own main NSO executable from the Switch release. The pinned setup script verifies its hash, uses 1.5.0 directly and converts listed 1.6.0 or 1.9.0 executables to 1.5.0 with a project-hosted patch; RomFS and other game content are not used. The About page says the project is useless to anyone who does not own the game.

The installation guide assumes Linux (native or WSL) or macOS and lists Python 3, Ninja, CMake, ccache, xdelta3, Clang and a Rust toolchain; the pinned CMakeLists requires CMake 3.30. Setup fetches Clang 4.0.1 for game code and installs tools/check. Submodules supply sead, agl, EventFlow, NintendoSDK headers and the shared nx-decomp-tools; the decompiling guide works from Hex-Rays or Ghidra output.

tools/check diffs each listed function against the original executable, and data/uking_functions.csv records its status. At the pinned commit that list marks 32,079 of 113,490 functions matching, 514 non-matching, 7,601 work in progress, 6,270 library and 67,026 not decompiled; the mutable botw.link badges showed 17.493% by size and 30.398% by function on review. This collection did not run the checker.

The pinned tree has no root license file and GitHub detects none, so no reuse license is stated; submodules and Nintendo content keep their own terms, and the About page calls the work a legal gray zone. AGENTS.md sets disclosure and human-review rules for AI-assisted contributions, but the reviewed files neither attribute the reconstruction to REA nor quantify AI use.

name: Skyward Sword: Wii decompilation with hash-checked relinking
description_en: Reconstructs C++ source for The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword’s Wii main.dol and REL modules, starting from the user’s NTSC-U 1.0 (SOUE01) disc files. Objects marked matching are compiled from source and linked with objects split from the original, and the result is checked against SHA-1 hashes; the repository ships no assets or assembly and is not a port.
description_zh: 以使用者自备的 NTSC-U 1.0（SOUE01）光盘文件为起点，为《塞尔达传说 天空之剑》Wii 版的 main.dol 和 REL 模块重建 C++ 源码。标为一致的对象由源码编译，再与从原文件拆分出的其余对象链接，并以 SHA-1 哈希校验结果；仓库不含素材或汇编，也不是移植。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress Wii decompilation whose only supported version is SOUE01 (NTSC-U 1.0); configure.py also lists SOUP01, but the pinned tree has configuration only for SOUE01. The output is a rebuilt main.dol and REL set for the Wii, not a PC executable or port.

Building needs the user’s own SOUE01 game: README names sys/main.dol and files/rels.arc from its data partition as the only required files. The repository contains no game assets or assembly; decomp-toolkit splits the user’s files into objects locally, using the input hash and split tables in config/SOUE01.

Builds run natively on Windows with Python and ninja, or on Linux/macOS with ninja and the automatically downloaded wibo wrapper. configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.7.1, objdiff v3.4.1, binutils 2.42-1 and a 20250812 compiler bundle, selecting Metrowerks Wii/1.5 for most code and Wii/1.3 for most NW4R code; objdiff compares individual objects during development.

The default ninja target links source-built objects only for units marked Matching (493 in configure.py; 536 remain NonMatching) and uses the original extracted object for the rest, then checks main.dol and 636 RELs against build.sha1. A passing check shows output identity, not complete decompilation. decomp.dev’s report for the pinned commit lists 27.89% of code bytes and 33,940 of 76,968 functions matched; CI uses a private container holding game files, and this collection ran neither.
The repository carries CC0-1.0; that dedication does not cover Nintendo’s game, its files or the downloaded compilers. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: 2 Ship 2 Harkinian: a native Majora’s Mask port built on the decompilation
description_en: Builds native Windows, Linux and macOS versions of The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask from an adapted copy of the zeldaret/mm decompilation, with libultraship reimplementing N64 SDK functions. Game data comes from a user-supplied ROM and is packed into an archive that custom asset packs can override. It targets a playable PC port with enhancements, not a byte-identical ROM.
description_zh: 以改编自 zeldaret/mm 反编译的源码为基础，构建《塞尔达传说：姆吉拉的假面》的原生 Windows、Linux 和 macOS 版本，并由 libultraship 重新实现 N64 SDK 函数。游戏数据来自使用者自备的 ROM，打包为可被自定义素材包覆盖的存档文件。它面向带增强功能的可玩 PC 移植，而不是逐字节一致的 ROM。
requirements: The reviewed develop commit follows release 5.0.1 (2026-08-25), published as Windows, Linux and macOS archives; nightly CI builds are for playtesting and may have bugs and crashes. The repository’s decomp_diff.py describes its game sources as changed decompilation code compared with the official zeldaret/mm repository. Rendering uses DirectX 11, OpenGL or Metal.

No copyrighted assets are included: supply a supported copy of Majora’s Mask. The docs list SHA-1 hashes for NTSC-U 1.0 and NTSC-U GC versions. Built-in extraction turns the supplied game into an mm.o2r archive; custom .o2r or .otr packs go in a mods folder, and the README notes that fast64 does not fully support MM.

Source builds need the libultraship, OTRExporter and ZAPDTR submodules plus CMake. Windows uses Visual Studio 2022 with the v143 toolset, Python 3 and at least 8 GB of RAM; the Linux lists include GCC or Clang, Ninja, SDL2, libzip, spdlog, tinyxml2 and Opus/Vorbis libraries; macOS needs Xcode tools with SDL2, libpng, GLEW, Ninja, CMake, nlohmann-json and libzip.

The reviewed README and build guide report no matching, checksum or fidelity checks for the port; the release notes list tweaks and bug fixes. Enhancement and randomizer code changes behavior relative to the original game. This collection did not build or run it.

The repository is CC0 1.0, and the libultraship submodule is MIT; game content from the user’s copy keeps its own rights, and the README says the project does not condone piracy. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: Ship of Harkinian: a native Ocarina of Time port built on the decompilation
description_en: Builds Ocarina of Time as a native PC application from the OoT decompilation’s source, with libultraship standing in for the N64 libultra SDK and DirectX 11, OpenGL or Metal rendering. No game assets are shipped: they are converted from the user’s supported ROM into an .o2r archive, and the port adds save states, alternate and custom assets and other enhancements.
description_zh: 以《时之笛》反编译项目的源码为基础，将游戏构建为原生 PC 程序，用 libultraship 替代 N64 的 libultra SDK，并以 DirectX 11、OpenGL 或 Metal 渲染。不随附游戏素材，而是从使用者自备的受支持 ROM 转换生成 .o2r 归档；移植版还加入了即时存档、替换与自定义素材等增强功能。
requirements: README presents Ship of Harkinian as built on libultraship and dependent on source from the OoT decompilation project; the soh/src tree carries that decomp-derived game code. The output is a modified native port (CMake project version 9.3.0) with added features, not a matching ROM build or a byte-for-byte reconstruction.

Play requires a legally acquired, supported Ocarina of Time ROM; docs/supportedHashes.json lists 19 SHA-1 entries covering PAL, NTSC (US/JP), GameCube, Master Quest and debug variants. Copyrighted assets are not included and are converted from that ROM into oot.o2r or oot-mq.o2r; prebuilt releases still need the ROM.

README documents Windows, Linux (AppImage) and macOS releases with DirectX 11, OpenGL or Metal; CMake also has Nintendo Switch and CafeOS (Wii U) branches. Source builds need CMake 3.26+, Python 3, Git and the libultraship and Torch submodules, plus Visual Studio 2022 (v143) on Windows or the listed distribution packages and minimum GCC/Clang versions on Linux.

The reviewed CI workflow builds Windows, macOS and Linux packages and generates soh.o2r; it runs no gameplay or fidelity comparison against the original game. Behavior and enhancements are project-documented, and this collection built or ran nothing.

The pinned tree has no root license file and GitHub detects none; the randomizer’s 3drando component carries its own license, the submodules are separate repositories and Nintendo content keeps its own rights. README says the project does not condone piracy; the reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: The Minish Cap: a GBA decompilation targeting five ROMs
description_en: Recreates a C source base for The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap from information in the game and static or dynamic analysis, building five Game Boy Advance ROMs: USA, EU, JP and two demos. Each version takes its assets from a user-supplied original ROM, and normal builds check the output’s SHA-1 hash. The project remains a work in progress, and some parts of the ROM may not yet be shiftable.
description_zh: 依据游戏内信息和静态或动态分析，为《塞尔达传说：缩小帽》重建 C 源码库，可构建美版、欧版、日版及两个演示版共五个 Game Boy Advance ROM。每个版本的素材都来自使用者自备的原始 ROM，常规构建会核对产物的 SHA-1 哈希。项目仍在进行中，ROM 的部分内容可能尚不能移动。
requirements: README calls this a WIP decompilation whose codebase can still change drastically, and warns that some parts of the ROM may not yet be shiftable, so modifications can be difficult. Its targets are tmc.gba (USA, the default), tmc_eu.gba, tmc_jp.gba, tmc_demo_usa.gba and tmc_demo_jp.gba. The output is a GBA ROM, not a native PC port.
The repository includes no game assets. Each version to be built needs its own original base ROM matching the SHA-1 listed in INSTALL.md; the build derives its assets from that ROM.

Builds run on Linux, on macOS with the Xcode command line tools (GNU make and sed are recommended), or on Windows through WSL, WSL2 or Cygwin. They need build-essential, Git, Python 3 with pip and pycparser, CMake, libpng, an arm-none-eabi-gcc toolchain (standalone or devkitPro gba-dev) and pret’s separate agbcc compiler installed into the tree.

COMPARE runs the SHA-1 check for normal builds and is off for CUSTOM builds, which INSTALL.md requires after modifying the game. The Jenkins pipeline builds all five versions with ROMs held on its build agent and publishes progress from the USA map file. For the reviewed commit, the matching log counts all 647,908 USA code bytes as source by the script’s own rules, which also count asm/src, asm/lib and libc objects, but only 238,628 of 13,933,140 data bytes; this collection did not rebuild it.

The reviewed tree has no license file and GitHub detects no license, so reuse terms for the source are unstated; original ROMs, derived assets and agbcc keep their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Ocarina of Time: decompilation with MD5-checked ROM builds for 16 versions
description_en: Recreates a C source base for Ocarina of Time that rebuilds 16 Nintendo 64, GameCube and iQue Player ROM versions, using information from the game and static and dynamic analysis. Assets come from the user’s own ROM and each default build is checked against that version’s MD5; README states the project is not producing a PC port and still calls the repository a work in progress.
description_zh: 借助游戏本身的信息以及静态与动态分析，为《时之笛》重建 C 源码库，可重新构建 Nintendo 64、GameCube 和 iQue Player 共 16 个 ROM 版本。素材取自使用者自备的 ROM，默认构建会以对应版本的 MD5 校验；README 说明项目不制作 PC 移植，并仍称仓库处于开发中。
requirements: README describes recreating a source base from scratch using information inside the game and static and/or dynamic analysis, and states that it is not producing a PC port. It builds 16 N64, GameCube and iQue Player ROM versions (default gc-eu-mq-dbg); some ROM parts may not yet be shiftable, so modding can be difficult.

Each build needs the user’s own base ROM for the chosen version, matching an MD5 listed in README; the repository includes no game assets and extracts them from that ROM during setup. Native ports such as Ship of Harkinian, and recompilation projects, are separate from this repository’s output.

README documents Linux or WSL builds, with separate macOS and Docker guides, needing Git, build-essential, curl, Python 3.10+ with pip and venv, libxml2 and a MIPS binutils toolchain. N64 and GameCube code builds with IDO 7.1 and 5.3 through ido-static-recomp; iQue builds also use EGCS for some files, and an optional GCC build is non-matching.

With the default COMPARE=1, make checks the built ROM’s MD5 against the version’s checksum file and prints OK or FAILED; NON_MATCHING=1 or COMPILER=gcc turns the check off. GitHub Actions, using a private container holding the base ROMs, reported all 16 version builds successful for the pinned commit, and the mutable progress badge read 100% on review. This collection ran no build.

The pinned tree has no license file and GitHub detects none, so no reuse license is stated; Nintendo content and compiler components keep their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: BaoCut Design: porting reconstructed canvas and design-system editors
description_en: Documents BaoCut’s design-canvas and design-system editors, which the project says it ported 1:1 from TypeScript reconstructions of Claude Design’s editors and hosts in agent sessions with annotation and export. Its runtime notes record identifier fixes checked against the original scripts and a structural comparison matching 19,111 of 20,463 canvas main-page functions. Unreviewed differences, the unpublished reconstruction record and reuse rights remain open; no hosted-backend recovery is claimed.
description_zh: 记录 BaoCut 的设计稿（画布）与设计系统编辑器；项目称其按 1:1 移植自 Claude Design 编辑器的 TypeScript 重建，并在智能体会话中提供标注与导出。运行时说明记录了对照原脚本修正的标识符，以及画布主页面 20463 个函数中有 19111 个结构完全一致的比对结果。未审阅的差异、未公开的重建记录及复用权利仍待确认；不主张恢复任何托管后端。
requirements: This entry covers the design-canvas and design-system editors added in the pinned commit, not the whole BaoCut product or its separately curated Slides editor. The runtime READMEs say both are ported 1:1 from separate TypeScript reconstructions of the original editor types (src/design-type, src/design-system-type), keeping file formats, UI, behavior and module structure, with BaoCut hosting changes marked by BaoCut: comments. Those reconstruction projects, their notes and evidence are not in this repository, and the sources name no exact original release.

Hosting changes replace the original globalThis.claude host interface with BaoCut shims, empty the parent-origin allowlist, disable analytics, and drop rooms, sampling and hosted design-system installs. The port omits Anthropic Sans in favor of system fonts but still inlines the original Anthropicons icon font, whose distribution license the READMEs call unconfirmed and slated for replacement. Use independently authorized design content and assets.

Building the editors needs Node.js >=22.12.0, npm workspace dependencies and the apps/design-editor and apps/design-system-editor builds. The canvas runtime keeps React 18.3.1 for artboards beside the workspace’s React 19, with Babel standalone 7.29.0, happy-dom, jQuery and dom-to-svg; full BaoCut source builds also need Rust, CMake and platform build tools. Agent-made designs use BaoCut’s built-in design and design-system skills through a configured local agent CLI such as Codex, under its own account and service terms.

The design-runtime README reports identifier fixes checked against the original scripts, then Babel-based structural fingerprints matching 19,111 of the original canvas main page’s 20,463 functions exactly; remaining binding-only differences fall in dependencies, while 1,019 structurally different innermost functions and renamed property-scrubber internals remain unreviewed residual risk. Published tests cover canvas checks, file routes and grants, downloads and annotation targets, and acceptance cases UI-11–UI-13 describe manual Web/desktop flows. None is a behavioral oracle against the original service; this collection did not run them.

The root BaoCut Community License 1.0 is source-available: personal, internal and content-creation uses are permitted, while commercializing BaoCut or its code needs a separate license. Third-party notices cover bundled npm packages but do not establish reuse rights in the reconstructed Claude Design code or the icon font. The author’s post does not name REA for this port, and a later third-party post’s REA claim is not confirmed by the author or the repository. This review read pinned sources without running the editors, agents or tests.

name: Project Arwing: Star Fox recompiled from a matching disassembly
description_en: Disassembles Star Fox’s 65816 and SuperFX code from runtime coverage and recursive descent, reassembles it into the original ROM, then translates it statically to C on a from-scratch SNES runtime for Windows, macOS and Linux. Code never reached in recorded sessions, and RAM code that no longer matches the ROM, falls back to an interpreter; the README reports identical per-frame hashes for both paths. The generated C is a mechanical translation rather than hand-decompiled source, and results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 依据运行覆盖率和递归下降反汇编 Star Fox 的 65816 与 SuperFX 代码，重新汇编出与原 ROM 一致的文件，再静态翻译为 C，运行于从零编写的 SNES 运行时，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。录制会话中未执行到的代码，以及与 ROM 不再一致的 RAM 代码，回退到解释器执行；README 报告两条路径的逐帧哈希一致。生成的 C 是机械翻译而非手工反编译的源码，结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: README reports a byte-identical ROM rebuild, 34,472 65816 and 14,577 SuperFX instructions, and 99.4% CPU / 100% SuperFX dispatches running recompiled over 20k gameplay frames. It lists the intro, title, training, Corneria and other levels reached by random play as playable. Labels are auto-generated, unreached code remains data run by the interpreter, and audio was checked only indirectly, not against hardware.

Supply your own Star Fox (USA) (Rev 2) ROM matching the SHA-1 in README; other revisions and regions are untested. Graphics, models and music are extracted from it at build time. The source build expects a headerless image, while the installer strips a 512-byte copier header. No game data is included.

Releases target Windows x64, macOS 11+ (not notarized) and Linux x86_64/ARM64 AppImages. Source builds need Python (3.10+ on Windows) with Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, Xcode command-line tools and SDL2, or gcc, SDL2, FreeType and DejaVu fonts; tools/build.py chains extraction, assembly, recompilation and compilation.

tools/build.py compares the reassembled ROM’s SHA-1 but only warns on a mismatch. The documented contributor check diffs --hashlog output from recompiled and --interp runs. CI assembles and recompiles without a ROM, zero-filling data, so it confirms neither matching nor gameplay; this collection did not rerun any check.

MIT covers tools/, src/, installer/, res/ and the build scripts; LICENSE excludes asm/, a disassembly of Nintendo's Star Fox code, and anything extracted from a ROM. This is an unofficial fan project unaffiliated with Nintendo. The reviewed repository makes no AI or REA attribution, so a circulating post's account of Opus 5.5 and a single prompt is unconfirmed here.

name: Project Arwing (2): Star Fox 2 recompiled from a matching disassembly
description_en: Rebuilds Star Fox 2 from a coverage-seeded 65816 and SuperFX disassembly that reassembles to the original ROM, then translates it statically to C for native Windows, macOS and Linux builds. Unreached code and RAM code that differs from the ROM run through an interpreter, and the README reports identical per-frame hashes against interpreted runs. It accepts the SNES Classic release image, not the 1995 prototypes; results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 从以运行覆盖率为种子的 65816 与 SuperFX 反汇编重建 Star Fox 2：反汇编可重新汇编为与原 ROM 一致的文件，再静态翻译为 C，生成原生 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 版本。未执行到的代码及与 ROM 不一致的 RAM 代码由解释器执行，README 报告其与解释运行的逐帧哈希一致。项目接受 SNES Classic 版映像，不支持 1995 年的原型版；结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: README reports a byte-identical ROM rebuild, 66,520 65816 and 23,186 SuperFX instructions, and 99.7% CPU / 100% SuperFX dispatches running recompiled over 20k gameplay frames, listing intro, title, menus, map and missions as playable. Labels are auto-generated, unreached code stays as interpreted data, and audio was checked only indirectly. README says Smooth mode removes slowdown but, unlike the Star Fox project, adds no interpolated 60 fps frames yet.

Supply your own Star Fox 2 ROM from the SNES Classic / Mini release, matching the SHA-1 in README; the 1995 prototypes will not work. Graphics, models and music are extracted from it at build time, and battery saves are written beside the rebuilt ROM. No game data is included.

Releases target Windows x64, macOS 11+ (not notarized) and Linux x86_64/ARM64 AppImages. Source builds need Python (3.10+ on Windows) with Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, Xcode command-line tools and SDL2, or gcc, SDL2, FreeType and DejaVu fonts; tools/build.py chains extraction, assembly, recompilation and compilation.

tools/build.py compares the reassembled ROM’s SHA-1 but only warns on a mismatch, and the documented contributor check diffs --hashlog output from recompiled and --interp runs. HD 3D hooks one of several projection routines and recovers sub-pixel positions for about 66–90% of vertices. This collection did not rerun these checks.

MIT covers tools/, src/, installer/, res/ and the build scripts; LICENSE excludes asm/, a disassembly of Nintendo's Star Fox 2 code, and anything extracted from a ROM. This is an unofficial fan project unaffiliated with Nintendo. The reviewed repository makes no AI or REA attribution, so a circulating post's account of Opus 5.5 and a single prompt is unconfirmed here.

name: Little Planet: Sonic CD recompiled from a matching disassembly
description_en: Disassembles every executable file on the Sonic CD disc from runtime coverage and recursive descent, reassembles them byte-identically, and translates the code statically to C on a from-scratch Mega-CD runtime that replaces the BIOS with a high-level implementation. Recompiled blocks run only where memory still holds the code they came from, and a script compares 96 stage runs frame by frame against the interpreter. The project also patches in widescreen and per-zone saves; results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 依据运行覆盖率和递归下降，反汇编 Sonic CD 光盘上的全部可执行文件并逐字节一致地重新汇编，再将代码静态翻译为 C，运行于从零编写、以高层实现替代 BIOS 的 Mega-CD 运行时。重编译代码块只在内存仍为其来源代码时执行，并有脚本以 96 段关卡运行逐帧对照解释器。项目还以补丁加入宽屏和逐区存档；结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: README reports that all 112 executable files reassemble byte-identically to the Japanese release, that 622k instructions recompile into 22,897 blocks, and that boot, gameplay, audio and bit-exact save states work. The disassembly is code only; graphics, sound and level data stay on the user’s disc. True16:9 widescreen and saves after every zone patch the game’s own programs, so those options depart from the original game.

Supply your own Sonic CD disc image (cue/bin, iso, ccd/img/sub, chd, or cue with compressed audio). The Japanese G-6021 release, identified by a data-track SHA-1 in README, is the tested one; other releases boot but are untested. No BIOS dump is needed, and no disc data is included.

Releases target Windows x64 (installer or portable zip), macOS 11+ (not notarized) and Linux x86_64/ARM64 AppImages. Source builds need Python (3.10+ on Windows) and SDL3, with Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, Xcode command-line tools or gcc/g++. The optional remastered opening also needs a separately built FFmpeg and a fetched video.

README documents tools/decomp.sh for extracting the disc, reassembling asm/ and comparing each file; tests/rc_check.sh compares per-frame RAM and CPU-PC hashes of recompiled and --interp runs across 96 scripted stages. README also reports SingleStepTests results: all 1.6M Z80 cases, and all 1M 68000 cases apart from some undocumented DIVS/ASR and address-error cases. CI tests only a homebrew test disc; this collection ran nothing.

MIT covers the runtime, tools and installer. third_party/ code, the bundled LGPL 2.1 FFmpeg and LuanUP’s remastered opening, included with permission, keep their own terms, and nothing extracted from a disc is covered. The reviewed LICENSE’s exclusion note names Star Fox 2 rather than Sonic CD. The project is unofficial, unaffiliated with Sega, and makes no AI or REA attribution.

name: vf2-decomp: differentially validated Virtua Fighter 2 recovery
description_en: Recovers Virtua Fighter 2 Version 2.1’s Sega Model 2A i960 program into portable, non-matching C17, accepting each recovered path only when it matches a reference i960 executor at controlled boundaries. The repository adds ROM validation, i960 and 68000 analysis tools, a bounded Model 2A hardware model and snapshot-based differential runners. README states that it is not yet a playable port; match flow, combat, physics, AI, rasterization and much of the audio remain open.
description_zh: 将 Virtua Fighter 2 Version 2.1 的 Sega Model 2A i960 程序恢复为可移植、非一致性的 C17 代码，每条恢复路径须在受控边界上与参考 i960 执行器一致才被接受。仓库还提供 ROM 校验、i960 与 68000 分析工具、有限范围的 Model 2A 硬件模型，以及基于快照的差分运行器。README 说明它尚不是可游玩的移植；对战流程、格斗、物理、AI、光栅化及大部分音频仍未完成。
requirements: README describes a clean-room, non-matching recovery whose native runtime preserves CPU, frame, counter and mutable-memory state through repeated scheduler and gameplay dispatches, including a 1,270,824-instruction post-scheduler corridor with no interpreted instructions. It explicitly does not claim complete decompilation, a playable executable, full Model 2/TGP emulation, SCSP DSP audio or every gameplay branch. Unverified paths fail closed with VF2_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED.

ROM-backed analysis and differential tests need a user-supplied, legally obtained copy of the supported arcade ROM set. config/vf2_v22_roms.csv records only filenames, sizes and hashes, and vf2rom verifies the set. The repository contains no Sega game data, and contributors must not commit ROMs or reconstructed region images.

Builds use CMake with a C17 compiler and warnings treated as errors, plus an optional sanitizer configuration. STATUS lists GCC/Clang CI, and README names native Windows MSVC as the canonical agent workflow. Setting VF2_ROM_DIR enables the ROM-backed CTest targets; otherwise only ROM-independent tests run.

The vf2i960 native-dispatch commands run the recorded differential milestones, and vf2cycles advances recovered C and the reference executor from a shared snapshot, stopping in strict mode at the first unsupported block, reference failure or state mismatch. STATUS reports MATCH for the third through sixth dispatches. CI runs only ROM-independent tests, so the ROM-backed results remain project-reported and were not rerun for this collection.

BSD-3-Clause covers the project’s code; MAME and public Intel i960 documentation serve as cross-references, not included source. docs/LEGAL.md discloses 301 original Sega symbol names, taken from a later Model 2 port DLL, as non-clean-room naming, and an untracked Sonic The Fighters disassembly is used only as a navigation aid. AGENTS.md addresses coding agents, but the reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: z2rs: an incremental Rust reconstruction of Zelda II checked against an emulator
description_en: Rebuilds Zelda II: The Adventure of Link (NES) in Rust for desktop, browser and Android by replacing the game’s 6502 routines one at a time. A built-in interpreter still runs the user’s ROM and hands ported routines to Rust, while a verifier compares RAM, sprites, palette and frames with a reference emulator. It is a behavioral, clean-room-style reconstruction guided by a community disassembly, not a decompilation or a finished standalone engine.
description_zh: 以 Rust 重建 NES 游戏《塞尔达传说 II：林克的冒险》，逐个替换游戏的 6502 例程，可运行于桌面、浏览器和 Android。内置解释器仍执行使用者的 ROM，并把已移植例程交给 Rust 实现；验证工具将 RAM、精灵、调色板和画面与参考模拟器逐帧比较。它是参考社区反汇编、以行为为准的类净室重建，而不是反编译，也还不是独立完整的引擎。
requirements: The reviewed commit is release v0.5.2 (2026-10-10), with Linux, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows archives plus an Android 8.0+ APK; z2rs.com hosts the browser build. PROVENANCE.md says it is not yet a standalone reimplementation: ported routines register in trap tables and the rest of the ROM is interpreted. The pinned ports.toml still marks all 2,960 routines unported, so it does not document how much logic runs as Rust.

Only the No-Intro USA dump is accepted, identified by the hash of the ROM body without its 16-byte iNES header (CRC32 BA322865). Graphics, maps, text and music are read from that ROM at run time, and nothing from the game is in the repository. Co-op, widescreen, HD packs, the randomizer and other enhancements are optional additions; Android lacks online co-op, the randomizer and enhancements.

Source builds need stable Rust; the browser build adds the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and wasm-pack, Android adds the SDK, NDK and cargo-ndk, and the default desktop netplay feature needs a C compiler. Release archives are not code-signed. Online co-op uses a public signalling server by default, and the desktop build shows Discord presence unless it is turned off.

z2-verify runs the ROM in tetanes-core 0.15 beside z2rs with identical input and compares RAM, battery WRAM, sprite OAM, palette and framebuffer after every frame, with two documented edge allowances for that emulator. Long tests replay TASVideos movies downloaded separately, and ROM-dependent tests skip without their inputs. The reviewed workflow only packages releases; no published verification results were found, and this collection ran no checks.

The sole maintainer releases the code under MIT; vendored matchbox_socket is MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the game itself is not covered. Routine layout comes from the CC0 FiendsOfTheElements/z2disassembly submodule and Data Crystal notes; the project describes one maintainer working from that material, not a two-team clean room, and publishes only a snapshot of earlier private history. PROVENANCE.md does not describe the tools used to write code, so no AI or REA use is established.

name: sm64ex: an enhanced Super Mario 64 PC port from the decompilation
description_en: Builds native Super Mario 64 executables from decompiled source, extending the sm64-port fork of the n64decomp reconstruction with renderer, input, camera, save-format and external-data options. Game assets are extracted from the user’s own ROM at build time. It is a non-matching enhanced port, not a byte-identical ROM reconstruction.
description_zh: 基于反编译源码构建原生 Super Mario 64 可执行文件，在 n64decomp 重建成果的 sm64-port 分支之上，增加渲染器、输入、视角、存档格式和外部数据等选项。游戏素材在构建时从使用者自备的 ROM 中提取。这是非一致性的增强移植，而不是逐字节一致的 ROM 重建。
requirements: The reviewed nightly branch (last pushed 2024-12-17) describes itself as a fork of sm64-port/sm64-port, which GitHub records as a fork of n64decomp/sm64, the separately catalogued ROM reconstruction. The Makefile builds PC targets only: it defines NON_MATCHING and AVOID_UB and forces COMPARE to 0, so a successful build is not a matching-ROM result.

Supply an original Super Mario 64 ROM named baserom.<version>.z64 for each version built (us by default, jp or eu); extract_assets.py compares its SHA-1 with the bundled reference before extracting assets. The sh (Shindou) option skips extraction and is labelled experimental in the Makefile and broken in the wiki option table; a 2020 known-issues page reports buggy EU text and missing EU audio.

The README defers building to the wiki, whose pages cover Linux (Python 3.6+, SDL2, GLEW, host GCC toolchain), Windows through MSYS2, FreeBSD, Raspberry Pi and an Emscripten/WebGL target; cross-compiling for Windows from Linux or WSL needs MXE, and OSX_BUILD enables macOS fixes. Renderers are OpenGL 2.1, OpenGL 1.3, Direct3D 11 and Direct3D 12, the DirectX ones only on Windows.

The Jenkinsfile builds us, eu and jp and rebuilds us after each enhancement patch, all with comparison disabled; this checks that builds succeed, not output identity or gameplay equivalence. Options such as disabled draw distance, analog camera, texture fixes and cheats intentionally change behavior, and the wiki notes the draw-distance option may affect gameplay. This collection did not build or run the port.

GitHub detects no repository license and the reviewed tree has no root license file; bundled tools carry their own licenses, and the src/pc notice reproduces an n64-fast3d-engine license that forbids binary redistribution. Original Nintendo content is not supplied, and the README forbids uploading copyrighted assets. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: Ghostship: a libultraship native port of Super Mario 64
description_en: Builds Super Mario 64 as a native PC, Switch and Android program by compiling decompilation-style game source against the libultraship platform library. A bundled extractor converts the user’s US or Japanese ROM into an O2R archive at first launch or build time. The project ships modern renderers, configuration menus and mod-archive loading, not a matching ROM.
description_zh: 将反编译风格的游戏源码编译到 libultraship 平台库上，把 Super Mario 64 构建为原生 PC、Switch 和 Android 程序。附带的提取工具会在首次启动或构建时，把使用者自备的美版或日版 ROM 转换为 O2R 存档。项目提供现代渲染器、配置菜单和模组存档加载，而不是生成一致的 ROM。
requirements: The reviewed develop branch declares version 3.0.0, matching the latest “Alfa” release. Its src tree keeps the audio, engine, game, goddard and menu layout of the n64decomp/sm64 reconstruction, with port code under src/port, and two sampled source files closely follow their n64decomp counterparts with port changes. The README itself does not name an upstream decompilation, so that lineage is a review observation.

Supply your own Super Mario 64 ROM in .z64 byte order: the README accepts only the US and Japanese releases and lists their SHA-1 values. PC releases convert it to sm64.o2r; the Switch build reuses an O2R generated on PC, and the Android app checks the ROM hash and converts it on the device. No game data is bundled.

Source builds use CMake with the libultraship and Torch submodules: Visual Studio 2022 with the v143 toolset, Python 3 and CMake on Windows, or GCC/Clang, Ninja, SDL2, libzip and the listed libraries on Linux. Renderers are DirectX 11, OpenGL, Metal and Vulkan where drivers allow. The building guide still names sf64.o2r and 2s2h.elf from other Harbour Masters ports, so its file names need checking against the current targets.

GitHub Actions workflows build Windows, macOS, Linux, Switch and web packages. The README calls CI builds playtest-only and warns of bugs and crashes. No matching, regression or original-hardware comparison result is published, and this collection did not build or run the port.

The root LICENSE.md is MIT (2026, Lywx) for the project’s own code. Submodules keep their own terms, and Nintendo’s code-derived content and ROM assets are not licensed by it; the README says it does not condone piracy. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: Super Mario Sunshine: an in-progress matching GameCube decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs Super Mario Sunshine’s C++ source so that the original Metrowerks compiler reproduces byte-identical object files for four GameCube releases and the Switch 3D All-Stars build. The target binary comes from the user’s own disc image, and objdiff compares rebuilt objects function by function. The work is incomplete, and the repository publishes contribution rules for AI agents alongside its human workflow.
description_zh: 重建 Super Mario Sunshine 的 C++ 源码，目标是让原版 Metrowerks 编译器为四个 GameCube 发行版本及 Switch 版 3D All-Stars 生成逐字节一致的目标文件。目标二进制取自使用者自备的光盘镜像，objdiff 按函数比对重建出的目标文件。工作尚未完成，仓库在人工流程之外还发布了面向 AI 智能体的贡献规则。
requirements: The README calls this a work-in-progress decompilation. configure.py defaults to GMSJ01 (JPN Rev 0) and also targets GMSP01, GMSE01, GMSJ01 Rev 1 and the GMSP01_NX build from Super Mario 3D All-Stars. Only objects marked Matching are linked by default; --non-matching links equivalent or modded objects. For GMSJ01 at the reviewed commit, decomp.dev reported 49.51% of code decompiled and 18.42% fully linked; this collection did not recompute those figures.

Copy your own disc image for each version into orig/<version>. ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ and TGC images are accepted, and the repository says it contains no game assets or assembly. The GMSJ01 symbol configuration is generated from the mario.MAP linker map found on that disc; the CI workflow notes that GMSE01 has no MAP file and skips symbol-order checks for it.

Builds need Python and Ninja on Windows, macOS or Linux; the build fetches decomp-toolkit, binutils and retro Metrowerks compilers (GC 1.2.5 for most code), and runs them through the wibo wrapper on macOS and Linux. objdiff compares rebuilt objects with those extracted from the original DOL, and each version’s build.sha1 records the target DOL hash.

AGENTS.md requires ninja baseline and changes_all regression reports for all five versions, each still reporting its DOL as OK. CI builds every version in a build container that supplies the original files and checks symbol order for changed units. These are project-reported checks and progress figures, not evidence of a complete or playable rebuilt game; no build was run here.

AGENTS.md, symlinked as CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md, sets workflows for AI agents. It bars unsupervised agents from MSL, MetroTRK, THPPlayer, Dolphin SDK and JSystem code and defers hard judgment calls to humans, but it does not quantify agent-written code. The repository declares CC0-1.0; Nintendo’s game, disc contents and the downloaded compilers keep separate rights. No REA use is established.

name: Dusklight: a native Twilight Princess port built on the decompilation
description_en: Reimplements Twilight Princess as a native application for desktop and mobile platforms, building on the zeldaret/tp decompilation and the Aurora GameCube/Wii compatibility layer. It runs from the user’s own disc image with no bundled assets and aims to stay accurate to the original while adding options, enhancements and mods.
description_zh: 以 zeldaret/tp 反编译项目和 Aurora GameCube／Wii 兼容层为基础，将《塞尔达传说 黄昏公主》重新实现为桌面与移动平台的原生应用。程序读取使用者自备的光盘镜像运行，不附带任何素材；项目力求忠于原作，同时加入新选项、增强功能和模组。
requirements: README calls Dusklight a reverse-engineered reimplementation that aims to be as accurate as possible while adding options, enhancements and tools. It is based on the zeldaret/tp decompilation, which README says is matching only for GameCube, so Wii discs still show the GameCube HUD and other GameCube specifics. This is a modified port, not a matching rebuild of the original executable.

No copyrighted assets are provided: the user supplies a dump of their own disc, and README says every commercial disc except the Korean Wii release is supported. The executable reads ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO and GCZ images directly.

Runtime needs a GPU with D3D12, Vulkan 1.1+ or Metal; D3D11 and Android OpenGL ES are best-effort without full accuracy or performance. The pinned tree has Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, tvOS and Android platform folders, and CI builds Linux, macOS, iOS, Android and Windows targets. Source builds need CMake 3.25+, Python 3, the listed per-OS toolchains and recursive submodules, including Aurora.
The reviewed CI workflow builds packages but runs no comparison against the original game. Accuracy and enhancement claims are project-reported, and this collection built or ran nothing.

LICENSE.md is CC0-1.0; it does not cover Nintendo’s game or disc content, and submodules such as Aurora and the randomizer mod are separate repositories. README says the project does not accept primarily AI-generated contributions and warns of unaffiliated sites spreading AI-generated misinformation; the reviewed sources establish no REA involvement.

name: Metaforce: a Metroid Prime engine reimplementation rebuilt on the decompilation
description_en: Started in 2015 as a reverse-engineered reimplementation of the Metroid Prime engine, Metaforce has been rewritten on top of the PrimeDecomp matching decompilation. Its native app compiles that game code as non-matching C++ for desktop and mobile through the Aurora GameCube compatibility layer and loads a user-selected disc image. The README says builds are unavailable while the rewrite stabilizes.
description_zh: Metaforce 于 2015 年作为《密特罗德 Prime》引擎的逆向重实现项目启动，现已在 PrimeDecomp 一致性反编译之上重写。其原生应用借助 Aurora GameCube 兼容层，将这些游戏代码以非一致模式编译为桌面和移动端程序，并读取使用者选择的光盘镜像。README 表示重写稳定之前暂不提供构建版本。
requirements: README dates development to June 2015 by Cirrus and Antidote and says the project was recently rewritten on the PrimeDecomp matching decompilation; builds are unavailable while it stabilizes, although CI builds Windows, Linux, Apple and Android packages. The only GitHub release is a 2015 prerelease, so none corresponds to the rewrite. This is separate from Odrannnn/MetroidPrimePort, another native port built from PrimeDecomp.

The repository ships no game files; its orig/ version folders hold only placeholders. At startup the app takes or asks for a Metroid Prime disc image (ISO, GCM, CISO, GCZ, RVZ, WIA or TGC). CMake compiles the native target with TARGET_PC, NONMATCHING and VERSION=1, and configure.py names version 1 as the default GM8E01_00 (NTSC-U v1.088) build; the README lists no supported disc revisions.

Building needs CMake 3.25+, Python 3 and a recursive clone with the aurora, borealis and musyx submodules; Windows uses Visual Studio 2019 with the Clang and clang-cl components, macOS needs Xcode 11.5+, and Linux needs the listed Ubuntu, Arch or Fedora packages. README platforms are Windows 10+ (D3D12, Vulkan or D3D11), macOS 10.15+ (Metal), Linux (Vulkan), Android (Vulkan or OpenGL ES) and iOS (Metal); Android also needs SDK Platform 37, the NDK and JDK 17+.

configure.py still records per-object matching status across ten disc versions for the separate GameCube build, but CI ignores those files and builds only native packages. The reviewed sources publish no fidelity or gameplay checks for the native app, and this collection did not build or run it.

Metaforce contributors’ code is MIT, and a separate LICENSE.decomp carries CC0 1.0; the reviewed files do not say which directories each covers. Disc content keeps its own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: Super Mario Sunshine (USA): an AI-assisted matching decompilation fork
description_en: Extends the doldecomp Super Mario Sunshine decompilation to the North American GMSE01 release. The README says AI was used extensively, and the repository’s agent rules, work order and progress files describe batch-based Claude and Codex orchestration. Its rebuilt DOL is reported byte-identical, but unfinished objects are still linked from code extracted from the user’s disc.
description_zh: 将 doldecomp 的 Super Mario Sunshine 反编译工作扩展到北美 GMSE01 版本。README 称大量使用了 AI，仓库中的智能体规则、工作顺序和进度文件也记录了按批次编排 Claude 与 Codex 的方式。项目报告重建的 DOL 逐字节一致，但尚未完成的目标文件仍取自使用者光盘中提取的代码。
requirements: This hobby fork of doldecomp/sms targets GMSE01 (USA Rev 0). The README says it began when upstream’s Japanese decompilation was about 38% matched, and PROGRESS.md names upstream ab00c3c9 as its base. GMSJ01 and GMSP01 configs remain, but the README marks PAL as slightly broken and AGENTS.md says neither can be built or regression-tested in this clone.

Supply your own North American Rev 0 disc image in orig/GMSE01 (ISO, RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ or TGC). The GMSE01 build notes record the required extracted-DOL SHA-1. Those notes say the initial symbols came from a community-hosted marioUS.map that is not on the US disc, while AGENTS.md calls the US map a real map shipped on the disc; that provenance conflict is left unresolved here.

Builds use Python 3 and Ninja on Windows, macOS (with Wine Crossover) or Linux (wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere), plus the pinned decomp-toolkit and Metrowerks tools. The output is build/GMSE01/mario.dol, checked against the extracted original. Playing it still needs the original disc image in Dolphin; a separate native PC port uses this fork as its decompilation submodule.

The README (2026-09-29) reports 99.60% fuzzy, 73.65% byte-perfect and 34.79% source-linked code, with 12,052 of 12,904 functions exact and 542 of 732 objects linked; PROGRESS.md (2026-09-27) gives slightly lower figures. A byte-identical DOL therefore does not mean complete source. The fork’s CI matrix builds only GMSJ01, so GMSE01 results are locally reported, and none were rerun here.

AGENTS.md, symlinked as CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md, lifts upstream’s ban on autonomous library work. It requires agents to work only from the binary, the linker map and the repository, and forbids fakematches and leaked SDK sources. It does not measure how much code agents wrote. The repository keeps CC0-1.0, while Nintendo content and the compilers keep separate rights. No REA use is established.

name: Donkey Kong 64: Recompiled — an N64Recomp native port
description_en: Uses N64Recomp to statically recompile the US Nintendo 64 release of Donkey Kong 64 into a native port, with RT64 as the renderer. The port is not built from decompiled source, but borrows headers and some functions from the in-progress DK64 decompilation for patches and enhancements. Its recompiler configuration reads a checked-in symbol dump and the ROM rather than a decompilation ELF.
description_zh: 使用 N64Recomp 将美版 Nintendo 64《大金刚 64》静态重编译为原生移植版，并以 RT64 作为渲染器。该移植并非基于反编译源码构建，但借用仍在进行中的 DK64 反编译项目的头文件和部分函数来实现补丁与增强。其重编译配置读取仓库内的符号转储和 ROM，而非反编译生成的 ELF。
requirements: Plays only the user’s US Nintendo 64 Donkey Kong 64 ROM; other dump formats of that ROM are converted to .z64. The repository and releases contain no game assets, it is not an emulator for other ROMs, and the README describes modding and other-language support as future work.

Release v1.0.3 (2026-09-30) ships Windows, Linux x64/ARM64, Flatpak x64 and macOS ARM64 archives. The README requires a Direct3D 12.0 (Shader Model 6) or Vulkan 1.2 GPU and an AVX-capable CPU, and lists Intel GPUs on Linux, the prebuilt Linux binary on some distributions, and overlay software as known problems.

Source builds need a recursive clone, CMake and Ninja with Clang (Visual Studio 2022 with Clang and vcpkg curl on Windows), separately built N64Recomp and RSPRecomp, and a decompressed copy of the NTSC-U 1.0 ROM matching the SHA-1 in BUILDING.md; play still uses the standard ROM.

The README reports high-frame-rate, widescreen and input-lag improvements alongside cutscene edge quirks at very wide aspect ratios. It publishes no equivalence or gameplay test; pinned-commit CI only builds the port, with extra inputs from a secret-configured checkout. These claims were not rerun here.

GPLv3 project license; the original game, the decompilation submodule and other dependencies keep separate terms. CONTRIBUTING.md forbids AI-generated code contributions, and no REA or coding-agent involvement is established.

name: Twilight Princess: a decompilation with fully matching GameCube code
description_en: Reconstructs Twilight Princess source that compiles back to binaries identical to the originals, building GameCube, Wii and Nvidia Shield releases from one codebase through conditional compilation. README reports the GameCube code as completely matching but not every translation unit linked yet, with Debug and Wii alignment ongoing; the repository ships no assets or assembly and will not produce a port.
description_zh: 重建《塞尔达传说 黄昏公主》的源码，使其能重新编译出与原版一致的二进制文件；GameCube、Wii 与 Nvidia Shield 各版本通过条件编译共用同一套代码。README 报告 GameCube 版代码已完全一致，但尚未链接全部翻译单元，调试版与 Wii 版的对齐仍在进行；仓库不含素材或汇编，也不会制作移植。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress decompilation with ten listed targets: three GameCube releases (GZ2E01, GZ2P01, GZ2J01), five Wii builds including a kiosk demo, and two Nvidia Shield China builds. Output is the original platform’s executable and REL modules; README states the project will not produce a PC or other port, and Dusklight is a separate project built on this code.

Building needs the user’s own disc image of the chosen version in a supported format (ISO/GCM, RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ or TGC), which can be deleted after the first build. The repository contains no game assets or assembly; decomp-toolkit splits the original locally.

Builds run natively on Windows with Python and ninja, or on Linux/macOS with ninja and the automatically downloaded wibo wrapper. configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.8.0, objdiff v3.6.1, binutils 2.42-1 and a 20251118 compiler bundle, selecting Metrowerks compiler versions per target and library; objdiff provides per-object diffing.

The default build links source-built objects for units marked complete and original extracted objects for the rest, then checks the output against each version’s build.sha1 (758 entries for GZ2E01). decomp.dev’s reports for the pinned commit list 100% of code matched for all three GameCube versions, with 2,583 of 2,608 units complete, against 54.47% for ShieldD and 47.06% for Wii RZDE01_00. CI runs in a private container holding game files; this collection ran no build.
LICENSE.md is CC0-1.0; it does not cover Nintendo’s game, disc content or the downloaded compilers. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night: matching decompilation across PlayStation, PSP and Saturn builds
description_en: Recreates C source for Castlevania: Symphony of the Night from its PlayStation, PSP and Saturn binaries, aiming for code that compiles byte for byte to the original game files. The work-in-progress build combines decompiled code with assets and assembly extracted from a user-supplied disc image, then checks per-version SHA-1 hashes. Native PC experiments in the same tree are documented as unfinished and are not a released port.
description_zh: 从《恶魔城 月下夜想曲》的 PlayStation、PSP 和 Saturn 版二进制重建 C 源码，目标是逐字节编译出与原游戏文件一致的产物。这一进行中的构建将已反编译代码与从使用者自备光盘镜像提取的素材和汇编结合，再按版本检查 SHA-1 哈希。同一仓库中的原生 PC 实验被文档说明为尚未完成，并不是已发布的移植。
