requirements: README describes a work-in-progress matching decompilation of four builds: us (PlayStation SLUS-00067, the reference), hd (an unreleased Japanese PS1 build found in Castlevania: Dracula X Chronicles data), pspeu (the European Dracula X Chronicles release) and saturn (the externally developed Saturn port). The Build wiki notes that some non-matching functions remain behind a NON_MATCHING macro and are not guaranteed to be functionally equivalent. README links mutable progress pages on sotn.xee.dev and decomp.dev; this collection recorded no completion figure.

The repository includes no game assets and none of the assembly needed to compile; README requires a prior copy of the game. The Build wiki asks for an unmodified US PlayStation disc as BIN/CUE, while the pinned Makefile reads both PSP-derived builds from a European Dracula X Chronicles ISO and the Saturn build from a Saturn BIN/CUE, each placed under disks/ with a version-specific name.

The Build wiki is tested against Ubuntu 24.04 LTS in CI and also covers Windows through WSL 2 and Arch-based distributions; a Dockerfile provides an Ubuntu Noble environment. Builds need Go, Rust, Python 3.12+, MIPS and SH binutils, a MIPS GCC, ninja and submodule tools such as m2c, maspsx, asm-differ, mipsmatch and decomp-permuter. Project-hosted prebuilt archives, including cc1-psx, mwccpsp, a Cygnus 2.7 toolchain and wibo, are checked against SHA-256 files; the Saturn build also uses dosemu.

Unless SKIP_CHECK is set, the pinned build code hashes its outputs against config/check.<version>.sha, which lists main.exe, DRA.BIN, RIC.BIN and stage and overlay files for us and shorter lists for hd, pspeu and saturn. The wiki still names a make check step that the pinned Makefile does not define. These checks compare file identity for the supplied version, not gameplay coverage, and this collection did not rerun them.

The Makefile also accepts a pc version and src/pc holds native-port code, but the PC Port wiki page says no working end-to-end port based on the decompilation exists yet; no PC port is claimed here. The repository declares AGPL-3.0, while disc images, extracted assets and assembly, and the downloaded compilers keep separate rights. CONTRIBUTING allows coding-agent assistance only for changes contributors can justify and operate manually and requires commits and pull requests without autonomous tooling; this establishes no REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: LEGO Island, portable: a multi-platform port of the decompiled source
description_en: Adapts the LEGO Island decompilation into a portable build for desktop, mobile, console, DOS and Web targets. Windows-only subsystems are replaced with SDL3, miniaudio, iniparser and a custom Direct3D Retained Mode re-implementation, while core gameplay is meant to stay unchanged. It ports reconstructed source rather than checking byte-identical binaries, so it is distinct from the exact-rebuild decompilation case.
description_zh: 将 LEGO Island 反编译源码改造为可在桌面、移动设备、游戏主机、DOS 及 Web 上构建的移植版本。项目以 SDL3、miniaudio、iniparser 和自行重新实现的 Direct3D Retained Mode 替代仅限 Windows 的子系统，并力求保持核心玩法不变。它移植的是重建源码，而不校验与原版逐字节一致的二进制文件，因此有别于精确重构建的反编译案例。
requirements: README describes a portable version of English LEGO Island 1.1 built on isledecomp/isle, aiming at platform independence without gameplay changes or rewrites for their own sake, and the contributor guide accepts LEGO1 changes mainly when they serve platform compatibility. Light modding goes through extensions, which in the reviewed tree include multiplayer, a third-person camera and asset loaders. The status table lists Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, DOS, Web, iOS, Android, Xbox One, PlayStation Vita, Nintendo Switch and Nintendo 3DS.

An existing copy of LEGO Island is required. The guided installer asks for the retail CD-ROM or a disc image made from it and says any 1.0 or 1.1 retail version in any language works; its optional HD audio pack is limited to English 1.1. The installer describes the isle.pizza Web build as streaming the game without a local disc; this review did not examine what that site serves or on what basis.

Builds use CMake 3.25+ with a C++17 compiler; by default CMake fetches SDL3 and iniparser, and libsmacker and miniaudio are submodules. README points to the CI workflow instead of a separate build guide; that workflow uses MSVC, MinGW, macOS/Linux toolchains and platform SDKs such as Emscripten, devkitPro, VitaSDK, DJGPP and Android, and the desktop settings tool needs Qt 6. Release downloads are continuous builds of master, which README warns may regress.

The reviewed CI checks formatting and configures, builds and packages each platform target; it does not run the game or compare its behavior with the original. The per-platform status entries are CI badges, not gameplay-parity results. Kaitai Struct descriptions document save, animation, world-database and texture formats. This collection did not build or run the port.

The repository carries LGPL-3.0; bundled and fetched third-party libraries keep their own terms, and the original game data, LEGO trademarks and the bitmaps the installer takes from the original setup program retain separate rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution.

name: c1: a C port of PlayStation Crash Bandicoot
description_en: Ports the original PlayStation Crash Bandicoot game code to C function by function; its coding standard labels functions with the addresses of their original implementations. Only the PC build, using OpenGL, SDL2 and FluidSynth, currently works; it loads asset files from the user’s game disc and is only partially playable.
description_zh: 将 PlayStation 版《古惑狼》的原始游戏代码逐函数移植为 C 语言；其编码规范要求为函数标注原实现的地址。目前只有基于 OpenGL、SDL2 和 FluidSynth 的 PC 构建可用；它读取用户自备游戏光盘中的素材文件，仅能部分游玩。
requirements: The README reports the code as 100% ported but functionality at 78%. The tracked issue list includes crashes in several levels, incorrect camera and collision behavior, broken demo mode and title states, and behavior that changes under compiler optimization; the PlayStation (Psy-Q) build does not work.

Running needs the NSD/NSF asset files from the user’s own Crash Bandicoot disc; the repository ships no game data and the README does not name a supported disc region or version. The game boots into the title sequence unless a constant is changed and the code recompiled.

Only 32-bit x86 executables are supported, built with GNU Make and a 32-bit GNU toolchain (multilib GCC/G++ on 64-bit hosts) against OpenGL 2.0+, SDL2 and FluidSynth (cimgui is bundled). Compilation has been tested only on Ubuntu/Debian; there are no releases, and the last commit at review is 2024-01-22.

No byte-matching, equivalence or automated gameplay check is published, and the project status figures were not reproduced here. The repository has no license file, so reuse rights are unspecified, and the original game retains its own rights; no REA or AI involvement is documented.

name: Metroid Prime Port: an AI-assisted native port of the PrimeDecomp decompilation
description_en: Compiles the PrimeDecomp decompilation of Metroid Prime’s game and engine code as native C++20 for Linux, Windows and Android, with an experimental macOS build. Aurora supplies the GameCube SDK compatibility layer and rendering, and the port reads a user-supplied disc image at run time. The author states that parts were written with AI coding assistants under their oversight.
description_zh: 将 PrimeDecomp 对《密特罗德 Prime》游戏与引擎代码的反编译结果编译为原生 C++20 程序，支持 Linux、Windows 和 Android，另有实验性 macOS 版本。Aurora 提供 GameCube SDK 兼容层和渲染，移植版在运行时读取使用者自备的光盘镜像。作者声明部分代码是在其监督下借助 AI 编程助手编写的。
requirements: The reviewed port-branch commit is 16 commits after release v0.29.0 (2026-10-17), which ships Windows, Linux tarball, AppImage, Flatpak, Android and macOS arm64 packages; the macOS build is experimental and has not been played on a real Mac. The repository forks PrimeDecomp/prime and adds widescreen, uncapped frame rate, controls, save conversion, a randomizer and an Archipelago client. It does not link the separate DolRecomp recompilation experiment, and its decomp/ GameCube build is not used by the port.

No game content is included: supply a GameCube USA 1.00, 1.01 or 1.02 (GM8E01) or PAL (GM8P01) disc image as .iso, .gcm, .rvz, .wbfs, .ciso or .nkit. Japanese, Korean, Wii Trilogy and Remastered releases are not run as the base game; an experimental importer can read models and effects from the user’s own Remastered dump.

Builds need CMake 3.25+, Ninja, a C++20 compiler and a C23-capable C compiler for MusyX; Windows uses clang-cl from LLVM in an MSVC developer environment, and Android builds through Gradle. Configuring downloads about a dozen SHA-256-checked dependencies; Linux links several statically and then needs only OpenSSL 3 and the C/C++ runtime. The macOS app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized.

CI builds and runs the disc-free CTest port suite on Linux with GCC 14 and Clang 18 for pushes and pull requests; Windows and macOS workflows run weekly or by hand, and the Windows job also checks that the package reaches main and reports the missing disc. Opt-in real-disc smoke drivers cover lifecycle, mouse, area-reload and world-jump scenarios, with results reported by the author. The 1.00 sequence-break option restores named script locks, not missing 1.00 geometry; this collection did not build or run the port.

MIT covers only the project’s platform layer, scripts, tests, tools and docs. NOTICE says the game code in src/ and include/, the decompiled Dolphin SDK and the config/ symbol data derive from the retail executable, remain with their owners and are outside that grant, and that no game assets may be packaged; vendored and fetched components keep their own licenses. AI coding assistance is author-disclosed, and no REA use is established.

name: The Wind Waker: a GameCube decompilation with hash-checked relinking
description_en: Reconstructs source for The Wind Waker’s GameCube executable and REL modules across the USA/Korea, PAL and Japanese releases and a Japanese kiosk demo. Matched units are compiled from source and linked with objects split from the user’s disc, then checked against per-version SHA-1 hashes; the repository ships no assets or assembly and covers the GameCube game, not the HD remaster.
description_zh: 为《塞尔达传说 风之杖》GameCube 版的可执行文件和 REL 模块重建源码，涵盖美版／韩版、PAL 版、日版及日本体验版。已匹配的单元由源码编译，再与从使用者光盘中拆分出的对象链接，并按各版本的 SHA-1 哈希校验；仓库不含素材或汇编，范围是 GameCube 版而非 HD 重制版。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress GameCube decompilation supporting every GameCube version: GZLE01 (USA Rev 0 and Korea Rev 48), GZLP01 (PAL), GZLJ01 (Japan) and the D44J01 Japanese kiosk demo. Output is the original executable and REL modules, not a port; the reviewed sources do not cover the Wii U HD remaster.

Building needs the user’s own disc image of the chosen version in a supported format (ISO/GCM, RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ or TGC), which can be deleted after the first build. The repository contains no game assets or assembly; decomp-toolkit splits the original locally.

Builds run natively on Windows with Python and ninja, or on Linux/macOS with ninja and the automatically downloaded wibo wrapper. configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.8.3, objdiff v3.7.3, binutils 2.42-1 and a 20251118 compiler bundle; README also describes a shared Ghidra project as an aid whose output is not accurate enough to copy directly.

The default build links source-built objects only for units marked complete, uses original extracted objects for the rest and checks the result against the version’s build.sha1 (415–417 entries per version). decomp.dev’s reports for the pinned commit list 79.58% of GZLE01 code (32,968 of 39,324 functions) matched, 78.38–78.65% for the other retail versions and 74.08% for the demo. CI runs in a private container holding game files; this collection ran no build.

The repository carries CC0-1.0, which does not cover Nintendo’s game, disc content or the downloaded compilers. CONTRIBUTING.md rejects primarily AI-generated pull requests; the reviewed sources establish no REA involvement.

name: Sonic Mania: a game-code decompilation for the RSDKv5 engine
description_en: Reconstructs Sonic Mania’s game code in C and builds it with the separately decompiled RSDKv5 or RSDKv5U engine for Windows, Linux, Switch and Android. Assets must come from an official Sonic Mania (Plus) release; the project adds a mod loader and can build several retail versions. Its license describes the code as mostly functionally the same as the original, not byte-matching.
description_zh: 以 C 重建《索尼克狂欢》的游戏代码，并与另行反编译的 RSDKv5 或 RSDKv5U 引擎一起构建，支持 Windows、Linux、Switch 和 Android。素材必须来自官方发行的 Sonic Mania (Plus)；项目加入了模组加载器，并可构建多个零售版本。其许可证称代码大多在功能上与原作相同，而不是逐字节一致。
requirements: The repository describes itself as a complete decompilation of Sonic Mania (2017); its license says it also contains original code and that most code is expected to be functionally the same, so no byte-matching build is claimed. It adds a built-in mod loader and API and can build 1.00 (console launch), 1.03 (PC launch) and 1.06 (Plus update) variants. The reviewed commit is 15 commits after release v1.1.1 (2025-11-01).

It does not run without assets from an official Sonic Mania (Plus) release for Windows (Steam or Epic Games Store), Switch, PS4 or Xbox One; the Netflix Games version is not supported. By default it builds with the bundled RSDKv5 engine submodule at revision 3 (RSDKv5U) and game version 6, the last Steam release; with WITH_RSDK off it builds only the game code, and RETRO_DISABLE_PLUS is to be enabled for distribution builds.

Clone recursively, because GitHub’s source ZIPs omit the required submodules. CMake builds use Visual Studio with vcpkg (libtheora, libogg, GLEW, GLFW3, SDL2) on Windows, build tools with GLEW, GLFW and libtheora development packages on Linux, devkitPro packages for Switch, and the engine repository’s instructions for Android. GL builds need a user-made shader mod for videos and filters.

CI builds Windows x86 and x64 and Linux binaries against both the RSDKv5 and RSDKv5U configurations. The project publishes no comparison with the original binaries, and its FAQ says bugs present in official releases will mostly not be fixed. This collection did not build or run it.

The custom Sonic Mania Decompilation Source Code License v1 allows copying, modification and distribution only for non-commercial use, requires stating that the code is not the distributor’s, forbids distributing game assets other than unique modded ones, and binds forks to the same terms. Sega’s game and assets keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: MediEvil Recomp: a PlayStation static recompilation to C#
description_en: Statically recompiles the North American PlayStation release of MediEvil into C# with the RecompOne recompiler and runtime. The runtime stands in for BIOS, GPU, CD-ROM and other hardware services, and project patches change rendering, widescreen and terrain behavior. README stresses that this is a recompilation, not a decompilation, and labels it an open beta.
description_zh: 使用 RecompOne 重编译器及运行时，将北美版 PlayStation《MediEvil》静态重编译为 C# 代码。运行时代为提供 BIOS、GPU、CD-ROM 等硬件服务，项目补丁则修改渲染、宽屏和地形表现。README 强调这是重编译而非反编译，并将其标为公开测试版。
requirements: The reviewed tree targets the North American PlayStation release (SCUS-942.27); config/MediEvil.json lists the main executable and its overlays for RecompOne to translate. README calls this an open beta in which things will break, with stable 1.0 unreleased. The v0.2b changelog replaces the PGXP renderer with a native floating-point rendering patch and adds widescreen fixes and an automatic updater.

Requires a legally owned North American MediEvil disc in bin/cue or CHD form; README and disc/README.md name the two track .bin files and the .cue expected in disc/. The project does not supply game files. RecompOne states that its runtime needs no BIOS or other Sony files, only the game files.

Building needs Git with the pinned RecompOne and ShaderMod submodules and the .NET 10 SDK. Windows batch scripts or a manual RecompOne run against config/MediEvil.json generate the game code, which is then compiled as a .NET 10 application. Running needs the .NET 10 runtime, OpenAL and an OpenGL 2.1 GPU; v0.2b release packages cover Windows x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64 and Linux x64.

The build workflow recompiles and compiles the project using disc inputs from a separate access-restricted repository, then uploads the build; it does not run the game or compare behavior with the original. README credits references from an unnamed decompilation for function names and patches. This collection did not build or run the project.

MediEvilRecomp has no license file in the reviewed tree, so its reuse terms are unstated; the RecompOne submodule declares MIT. Original game content, including the executable code the recompiler translates, retains separate rights. Both READMEs state that no AI was used to write the code and that AI-generated contributions are rejected; this is not an REA-assisted case.

name: Crash Bandicoot 2 Recompiled: a PSXRecomp native build
description_en: A Windows launcher that uses the PSXRecomp recompiler and runtime to translate the user’s Crash Bandicoot 2: Cortex Strikes Back disc to C and compile it locally, so the game runs as native code with an emulated PlayStation hardware layer. The repository holds the launcher, a patched vendored runtime and a long bring-up log; it distributes no game code or data.
description_zh: 一个 Windows 启动器，借助 PSXRecomp 重编译器与运行时，将用户自备的《古惑狼 2》光盘转换为 C 代码并在本地编译，使游戏以原生代码配合模拟的 PlayStation 硬件层运行。仓库包含启动器、打过补丁的内置运行时以及详细的调试记录，不分发任何游戏代码或数据。
requirements: Needs a disc image the user owns of the North American release (serial SCUS-94154), as .cue/.bin or .chd; the launcher checks tracks, sectors and boot serial and hashes the image. No PlayStation BIOS is required because MIT-licensed OpenBIOS is included, and locally generated files derived from the disc must not be redistributed.

Release v0.9.6 (2026-10-08) is a 64-bit Windows 10+ bundle; a first build takes about 3 GB of disk space and five to twenty minutes. Source use needs Python 3.11+ with PySide6 and the PSXRecomp MinGW-w64 Clang toolchain; the notes say MSVC is unsupported, and 59 runtime patches are kept in tuning/patches.

The README calls the game completable from start to finish but a work-in-progress preview with minor sound and graphical issues. Streamed level-code overlays are compiled natively when possible and otherwise fall back to a MIPS interpreter; the opt-in 60 FPS mode runs the emulated CPU at 200% and is not verified across the whole game.

Published checks are launcher settings and UI smoke tests, scenario scripts and a harness comparing its own Direct3D 12 and OpenGL renderers; none claims equivalence with original hardware, and no result was rerun here.

There is no top-level license file. The README lists PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 for PSXRecomp, MIT for OpenBIOS, zlib for SDL3 and LGPLv3 for Qt/PySide6; the game and its trademarks belong to their owners. No REA or coding-agent involvement is documented.

name: Petari: a matching Super Mario Galaxy decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs Super Mario Galaxy’s Wii code as C++ that rebuilds, object by object, against main.dol files extracted from the user’s own Japanese, North American, PAL or Korean disc. Matched objects are linked from source and checked with objdiff and a target hash. The project describes itself as a work in progress, separate from any PC port, and says it does not accept AI-generated decompilation.
description_zh: 将 Super Mario Galaxy 的 Wii 代码重建为 C++，并以使用者从自有日版、北美版、PAL 版或韩版光盘中提取的 main.dol 为目标，逐个目标文件重建。已匹配的目标文件由源码链接，并通过 objdiff 和目标哈希检查。项目自称仍在进行中，与任何 PC 移植无关，并表示不接受 AI 生成的反编译代码。
requirements: configure.py targets RMGJ01, RMGE01, RMGP01 and RMGK01, defaulting to the Korean RMGK01 build. Only objects marked Matching are linked unless --non-matching is used. For the reviewed commit, decomp.dev reported 100.00% of RMGK01 code decompiled with 68.75% fully linked, and 99.70% decompiled for the other three versions, with 55.61–58.17% linked. These figures are project-tracker results, not a complete source-built game.

Extract your own copy of the game for the chosen region with Dolphin into orig/RMG<region>01; only sys/main.dol is needed. The repository says it contains no game assets or assembly. Each version’s config records the expected DOL SHA-1 in config.yml and build.sha1.

Builds need Python and Ninja on Windows, macOS or Linux; wibo runs the Windows tools on macOS and Linux. configure.py pins Metrowerks compiler packages from the GC 2.7–3.0a5.2 and Wii 1.0 families. The GitHub Actions workflow builds all four versions in a build container its comments call private. This collection did not build or diff the project.

CONTRIBUTING.md requires 1:1 matching for objects marked as decompiled, objdiff checks and a successful link. Every non-matching function in a pull request must link a decomp.me scratch, and decompiler output must not be copied directly. The README credits doldecomp bte, zeldaret tp (JSystem) and ogws as sources of code and headers.

The README states that AI or LLMs played no role in the decompilation and limits permitted AI use to cleanup, formatting, documentation and naming. That is a project statement, not something this review can verify. The repository declares CC0-1.0, while Nintendo content, extracted files and toolchains keep separate rights. No REA use is established, and the separate AstroCore PC port mentioned in the README has no public source here.

name: Wind Waker HD Recomp: a native port by static recompilation of the Wii U game
description_en: Statically recompiles The Wind Waker HD’s Wii U PowerPC code to C ahead of time, reimplements the Cafe OS libraries the game uses and implements GX2 graphics on Metal or Vulkan, producing native macOS, Linux, Windows and Android builds without a Cemu runtime. All game code and data are generated locally from the user’s own dump; an experimental macOS-only build can instead run functions from the separate ZeldaWWHDDecomp/wwhd decompilation.
description_zh: 将《塞尔达传说 风之杖 HD》Wii U 版的 PowerPC 代码预先静态重编译为 C，原生重新实现游戏所用的 Cafe OS 库，并在 Metal 或 Vulkan 上实现 GX2 图形，生成无需 Cemu 运行时的 macOS、Linux、Windows 和 Android 原生版本。所有游戏代码和数据都由使用者自己的转储在本地生成；另有仅限 macOS 的实验性构建，可改为运行独立的 ZeldaWWHDDecomp/wwhd 反编译中的函数。
requirements: README describes a static recompilation of the USA or European Wii U release (version 0, without the update) and reports the game playable from start to finish on macOS, Windows, Linux and Android. Known gaps include unimplemented geometry shaders and rectangle primitives and no controller rumble on macOS; true 60 fps is experimental. Unlike source decompilations such as zeldaret/tww, the default build runs machine-translated game code.

Needs the user’s own, legally obtained game: a .wud/.wux disc image with its disc key and the Wii U common key, a Cemu .wua archive, or an extracted game folder. Setup checks code/cking.rpx against the SHA-256 of each supported version. The repository and releases contain no game code, assets or keys, and the locally generated code and caches must not be redistributed.

Releases target Apple Silicon macOS 14+, Windows 10 1903+ or 11 on x86-64 or arm64, and glibc 2.35+ Linux on x86-64 or arm64, with Vulkan 1.3 (or 1.1/1.2 with VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering) where Vulkan is used; Android arm64 builds the game on the phone. First setup translates and compiles the code locally with a downloaded compiler (llvm-mingw on Windows, zig on Linux) or Apple’s command-line tools. Source builds need CMake 3.20+ and Python 3.

Reported checks are side-by-side rendering comparison with Cemu, players completing the game and, for the decompiled path, tools/verify’s function-by-function comparison of hand-written C++ with the recompiled original on generated and recorded inputs. The experimental decomp build (macOS, USA game only) runs 22,705 verified functions in 862 units at the pinned submodule. All results are project-reported; this collection ran nothing.

Project code is MPL-2.0; vendored Cemu code is MPL-2.0, while metal-cpp, {fmt}, Dear ImGui, zstd and the AppImage runtime components keep their own licenses, and the game remains Nintendo’s property. README calls it an unofficial fan project; the reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.

name: Castlevania 64: Recompiled — a beta static-recompilation port
description_en: Uses N64Recomp to statically recompile the US 1.0 Nintendo 64 release of Castlevania into a native PC port rendered with RT64. Game-specific C patches build against headers from a separate Castlevania 64 decompilation. A beta release tagged at the reviewed commit reports a working build with known issues, while the README there still describes an unfinished project.
description_zh: 使用 N64Recomp 将 Nintendo 64 版 Castlevania 美版 1.0 静态重编译为原生 PC 移植，并以 RT64 渲染。游戏专用的 C 补丁基于另一个 Castlevania 64 反编译项目的头文件构建。在所审提交上标记的测试版发布报告构建可用并列出已知问题，而同一提交的 README 仍称项目尚未完成。
requirements: The AppStream metadata describes Castlevania 64: Recompiled as an N64: Recompiled static recompilation into a native port using RT64 for rendering. The v0.5.0 beta release, tagged at the reviewed commit, calls itself a working build and lists known issues: Banjo Recomp assets still to be replaced, texture scrolls that do not animate above 30 FPS, and glitches in some looping animations. At the same commit the README still says the WIP recomp does not build, and BUILDING.md only says WIP.

The metadata says the original game is required. The launcher accepts a single entry, the US 1.0 release (game ID cv64.us.1.0) identified by a fixed ROM hash, and cv64.toml configures the NTSC 1.0 recompilation from a decompressed ELF plus an overlay list. CI copies that ELF and a decompressed ROM from a private repository through secrets; neither is in the public tree.

The CMake project needs CMake 3.20+, C++20 and the N64Recomp and RSPRecomp tools; the workflow pins an N64Recomp commit and builds Linux x64 and ARM64 AppImages, an x64 Flatpak, Windows and macOS targets. Patches compile as MIPS code with clang and ld.lld against headers from the k64ret/cv64 decompilation submodule, with symbol dumps from CV64Syms and submodules for N64ModernRuntime, RecompFrontend and RT64. Several sources and functions still carry Banjo names.

GitHub check runs recorded for the reviewed commit report successful builds on those platforms. That shows the private inputs compile, not gameplay fidelity; no matching, test or performance results are documented. This collection did not download the release binaries or rerun any build.

COPYING is GPLv3 and the metadata declares GPL-3.0+; the original ROM and the dependencies keep their own terms. This is a static recompilation, not recovered authored source or a complete decompilation. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: RSDKv5 Decompilation: reconstructing Retro Engine v5 and v5U
description_en: Reconstructs the Retro Engine (RSDK) v5 and v5 Ultimate runtime, the engine that runs Sonic Mania’s game code, and builds it for Windows, Linux, Switch and Android. RSDKv5U can also run RSDKv3 and RSDKv4 games such as Sonic CD and Sonic 1 & 2. The project adds a mod loader, a shader compiler and extra Windows backends, and ships no game data.
description_zh: 重建 Retro Engine（RSDK）v5 及 v5 Ultimate 运行时，即运行《索尼克狂欢》游戏代码的引擎，可构建 Windows、Linux、Switch 和 Android 版本。RSDKv5U 还能运行 RSDKv3 与 RSDKv4 游戏，例如 Sonic CD 和 Sonic 1 & 2。项目增加了模组加载器、着色器编译器和额外的 Windows 后端，且不附带任何游戏数据。
requirements: The repository describes itself as a complete decompilation of Retro Engine v5 and v5Ultimate; its license says it also contains original code and that most code is meant to be functionally the same as the specified RSDK version, so no byte-matching build is claimed. RETRO_REVISION defaults to 3 (RSDKv5U). The reviewed commit is 13 commits after release v1.1.1 (2025-11-01).

Neither game data nor game logic ships here. The engine loads data files from an official RSDKv5(U) game such as Sonic Mania (Plus), and game code comes from a separate project linked as Game, such as the Sonic Mania decompilation, which also bundles this engine. The FAQ covers Sonic Origins data files, which lack the games’ music and sound effects, and notes that release builds block the Origins Plus characters.

Clone recursively, because GitHub’s source ZIPs omit the required submodules. CMake builds use Visual Studio with vcpkg on Windows, GLEW, GLFW and libtheora development packages on Linux, devkitPro packages for Switch, and a separate Android guide; community forks for WebAssembly, New 3DS, Wii U, Wii and Vita are listed as possibly WIP or outdated. The default Windows DirectX backends support only XInput controllers, and GL builds need a user-made shader mod for videos and filters.

CI builds Windows x86 and x64, Linux and Android binaries. The project publishes no comparison with the original engine binaries, and the FAQ says bugs present in official releases will mostly not be fixed. This collection did not build or run it.

The custom RSDKv5(U) Decompilation Source Code License v2.1 requires any distributed prebuilt executable to have DLC disabled by default, forbids commercial use and distributing game assets other than unique modded ones, requires crediting Evening Star and the decompilation authors Rubberduckycooly and chuliRMG, and binds forks to the same terms. The README says Evening Star owns the Retro Engine; the reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: C2C: hybrid recompilation and hand decompilation of Crash Bandicoot 2
description_en: An early reverse-engineering effort on PlayStation Crash Bandicoot 2 that converts the engine’s MIPS machine code directly into a very large C file and runs it against a modified PCSX-R emulator library for hardware I/O. Translated functions are meant to be decompiled by hand and moved into ordinary C, gradually replacing the mechanical translation.
description_zh: 一个早期的 PlayStation《古惑狼 2》逆向工程项目：把引擎的 MIPS 机器码直接转换为一个体量巨大的 C 文件，并调用改造后的 PCSX-R 模拟器库处理硬件 I/O。转换出的函数计划逐个手工反编译为普通 C 代码，逐步替换机械转换的部分。
requirements: Running needs the user’s own PAL Crash Bandicoot 2 disc as a raw BIN image with full sector headers and that disc’s SCES_009.67 executable, plus third-party PlayStation emulator GPU, SPU and two gamepad plugins and a 128 KB memory-card file; the repository ships no game data.

Windows only: the main program builds under Cygwin with GNU Make, GCC and SDL2, the emulator library needs Microsoft Visual C++ 2005 or later, and the optional C# disassembler needs Visual C# 2005 or later. Development ran on the develop branch from January to April 2015, and there are no releases.

The README warns that the software is not intended for regular use and reports no playability status. Its translator does little decompiling and does not resolve indirect branches or jump tables, so code regions must be listed by hand; docs/FUNCTIONS.md names 18 of 818 listed function entry points.

No matching or equivalence check is published, and nothing was built or run here. The repository has no license file; the PCSX-R-derived emulator sources carry GPL-2.0-or-later headers, and the original game retains its own rights. No REA or AI involvement is documented.

name: MediEvil decompilation: an early checksum-gated PlayStation project
description_en: Decompiles the US PlayStation release of MediEvil toward C source that rebuilds its main executable, game executable and 26 overlays. splat splits the user's own disc files, and the default build compares all 28 outputs with SHA-1 checksums. README describes the project as a work in progress and publishes no progress figure.
description_zh: 将美版 PlayStation《MediEvil》逐步反编译为 C 源码，目标是重新生成其主程序、游戏程序及 26 个覆盖模块。splat 拆分使用者自备的光盘文件，默认构建会将全部 28 个产物与 SHA-1 校验值比较。README 称项目仍在进行中，未公布进度数据。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress decompilation of the US PlayStation MediEvil 1, with MediEvil 2 left for later. The Makefile targets SCUS_942.27, MEDIEVIL.EXE and 26 overlay binaries. In the reviewed tree most functions are still included as split assembly through INCLUDE_ASM rather than written in C, README's progress section is a placeholder, and the pinned commit dates from 2026-02-23.

Requires files from the user's own US MediEvil disc in disk/; the splat configuration expects SCUS_942.27 with a fixed SHA-1, and make extract splits the executables and overlays from those files. The repository supplies no game files.

The build expects a Linux-style host: GNU make, mipsel-linux-gnu binutils, Python 3 with the listed packages such as spimdisasm and rabbitizer, and the splat, m2c, maspsx and asm-differ submodules. C files go through a bundled PlayStation GCC 2.8.1 cc1 binary and maspsx. README points contributors to wiki pages for setup, the rebase workflow and the decompilation process.

make all builds every binary and runs sha1sum against config/medievil.check.sha; CI runs extraction and that check using disc files from an access-restricted repository. A passing check shows that the assembled outputs match those checksums, not how much code has been decompiled to C or that gameplay was exercised. This collection did not build or run the project.

The repository declares MIT; original game content, the bundled compiler binaries and the PSY-Q headers and data in the tree retain their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and the project is separate from the MediEvil Recomp static recompilation.

name: Conker's Bad Fur Day: Recompiled — an N64Recomp native port
description_en: Statically recompiles the US Nintendo 64 release of Conker’s Bad Fur Day with N64Recomp into a native Windows, Linux and macOS port on N64ModernRuntime and RT64. Function names and boundaries come from a vendored, still mostly assembly decompilation, while the recompiled code is taken from the user’s ROM so unmatched decompiled C cannot change behavior. The author reports heavy use of Claude Code across the project.
description_zh: 使用 N64Recomp 将美版 Nintendo 64《Conker's Bad Fur Day》静态重编译为基于 N64ModernRuntime 和 RT64 的原生 Windows、Linux 与 macOS 移植版。函数名称与边界来自仓库内置、仍以汇编为主的反编译项目，而重编译的代码取自用户的 ROM，因此尚未匹配的反编译 C 代码不会改变游戏行为。作者称整个项目大量使用了 Claude Code。
requirements: Requires the user’s US ROM in big-endian .z64 form with the SHA-1 listed in the README; the repository and release packages contain no game data. ROM hacks that change only assets are accepted, while hacks that change code and other regions’ ROMs are refused.

Release V0.1.6 (2026-10-13) packages Windows, Linux and macOS builds plus a mods archive. Rendering uses Direct3D 12 or Vulkan on Windows, Vulkan on Linux and Metal on macOS; Linux builds are tested on Ubuntu 24.04, and the unsigned macOS release targets Apple Silicon with macOS 15 or later.

Source builds need a recursive clone, Git and Python 3 plus Visual Studio 2022+ on Windows, CMake, Ninja, Clang and SDL2 on Linux, or full Xcode and Homebrew on macOS, in a path without an apostrophe. N64Recomp and RSPRecomp run from a committed symbol file; regenerating it with the optional decompilation build also needs IDO and MIPS binutils.

The README reports the game played through to the end, with a widescreen pause-background issue; a macOS play-through is not yet confirmed and Intel Macs are untried. Decompiled C must rebuild the ROM’s code byte for byte, and the port is checked by play and by comparison with the original in an emulator; names are marked as guesses, and nothing was rerun here.

The author reports heavy Claude Code use for the recompilation setup, tool patches, host application, mods and decompiled functions; no REA use is documented. Own code is MIT, but builds including GPLv3 N64ModernRuntime are distributed under GPLv3, an RT64 patch is GPL-2.0-or-later, and the game is not covered.

name: ProjectCane: a native PC port of Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus
description_en: Rebuilds the NTSC PlayStation 2 release of Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus as a native C++ game for Windows and Linux, running on data extracted from the player's own disc image. The README reports the full game as playable while work continues on accuracy and remaining differences from the original. It does not describe its reverse-engineering method or relate the port to the separate sly1 decompilation.
description_zh: 将 PlayStation 2 版《Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus》美版重建为 Windows 和 Linux 上的原生 C++ 游戏，运行时使用从玩家自有光盘镜像中提取的数据。README 报告整部游戏均可游玩，同时仍在改进准确性并处理与原版的剩余差异。项目未说明其逆向工程方法，也未说明与另一个 sly1 反编译项目的关系。
requirements: README describes a complete, playable native port of the NTSC release for Windows and Linux, including Steam Deck, that began as a map viewer; the Beta 0.4.1 release is tagged one commit before the reviewed revision. Work is said to continue on accuracy, performance, controller support, platform compatibility and remaining differences from the PS2 release. The repository description says the port was rebuilt through reverse engineering, but the README gives no method, symbol source or comparison with the original.

No original game data is included. Players supply their own NTSC disc image, which the bundled extractor identifies by the serial SCUS-97198, and the extracted Worlds and Cutscenes directories must sit beside the executable. The Beta 0.4.1 notes say game data must be extracted again after that update.

Windows builds use Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ desktop workload, plus the .NET 9 SDK for the Avalonia-based extractor, or CMake presets. Linux builds need CMake 3.22+, Ninja, a C++20 compiler, pkg-config and FFmpeg development libraries; CMake fetches GLFW 3.4 and SDL2, and graphics use OpenGL through glad with Dear ImGui. Portable AppImages are built in Docker against an Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35 baseline.
No automated tests, matching checks or side-by-side comparisons are documented, so playability and fidelity remain project claims. This collection did not download releases or extract any disc.

No license file is present, so reuse terms for the source are unstated; Sly Cooper names and assets belong to their owners, and the README disclaims affiliation with Sony Interactive Entertainment and Sucker Punch Productions. The README also asks for Sly 2 or Sly 3 debug builds with symbols to support future ports. Reviewed sources establish no REA involvement, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Firefighter: a decompiled DOS game ported to Rust
description_en: Eric S. Raymond’s terminal port of Firefighter, Eben Sprinsock’s 1985 DOS shareware game. The project history says ChatGPT 5.5 decompiled the DOS binary to Borland Pascal and translated it to Rust, after which Raymond modernized the interface and corrected a scoring mismatch. Unchanged gameplay is the author’s statement; the intermediate Pascal and any comparison runs are not published.
description_zh: Eric S. Raymond 将 Eben Sprinsock 于 1985 年发布的 DOS 共享软件游戏 Firefighter 移植为终端游戏。项目历史记载，ChatGPT 5.5 先将 DOS 二进制反编译为 Borland Pascal，再译为 Rust；之后 Raymond 改进了界面，并修正一处计分不符。玩法未变是作者的说法；中间 Pascal 代码及任何对照运行均未公开。
requirements: The reviewed 1.2.0 release (2026-06-08) is a Rust terminal game for Unix-like systems: a 25×25 forest-fire board with easy, medium and hard modes, an optional RNG seed and mouse cursor movement. It needs a UTF-8 ANSI terminal of at least 80×25 with alternate-screen and raw-mode input; mouse movement also needs mouse reporting.

Build with Cargo (crossterm and rand); the Makefile wraps cargo build, installs the binary and renders the manual page with Asciidoctor. Building or playing the port needs no original DOS binary or game data; the history page links an Internet Archive copy of the shareware original.

The history lists the recovery steps: decompiling the DOS binary to Borland Pascal with ChatGPT 5.5, translating that to Rust, then adding interface changes, a seed option and a fix for per-difficulty maximum scores that did not match the score computation. The decompiled Pascal, prompts and original binary are not in the repository, so the decompilation itself cannot be inspected.

Verification is limited to make check (cargo check and clippy) and a few unit tests for option parsing, the display test pattern and maximum-score consistency. No comparison with the original program is published; unchanged gameplay logic is the author’s claim, and this review ran nothing.

COPYING is BSD-2-Clause, and source headers name Raymond and Sprinsock as joint copyright holders; the README says the port is released with the original author’s permission. The shareware original keeps its own rights. The reviewed sources credit ChatGPT and establish no REA connection.

name: flipper-telink: replacement firmware for Tuya Zigbee remotes
description_en: A Flipper Zero app that bit-bangs Telink’s SWire debug interface to dump and reflash TLSR825x Zigbee devices, with static-analysis notes on the dumps and freshly written firmware for two of them. For Tuya TS0044/TS0046 scene remotes, the notes trace the stock ~500 ms single-click delay to a double-click window; the replacement firmware drops that window while presenting the stock model IDs to Zigbee2MQTT. The latest Zigbee build is marked unverified for pairing, actions and battery reporting.
description_zh: 一款 Flipper Zero 应用，以位操作驱动 Telink 的 SWire 调试接口，用于转储并重刷 TLSR825x Zigbee 设备；仓库还附有对转储固件的静态分析笔记，以及为其中两款设备全新编写的固件。针对 Tuya TS0044/TS0046 场景遥控器，笔记将原厂约 500 ms 的单击延迟追溯到双击判定窗口；替换固件取消该窗口，同时向 Zigbee2MQTT 呈现原厂型号标识。最新 Zigbee 版本的配对、动作及电量上报被标注为尚未验证。
requirements: Hardware: a Flipper Zero on Unleashed firmware (the notes name API 87.8; apps built with the official SDK will not load), wired to the target’s SWS pin, ground and 3.3 V. The flasher app builds with ufbt and a project-local SDK; the firmware builds with the Telink Zigbee+BLE SDK in a Docker tc32 toolchain and, once installed, updates over BLE OTA.

Inputs are the user’s own devices and their flash dumps. dumps/ publishes sanitized stock images of four devices, with Zigbee network state and Tuya credentials blanked by tools/sanitize_dump.py; raw dumps stay private. Stock firmware rights stay with its vendors, and the repository states no terms for these images.

The TS0044/TS0046 notes derive GPIO roles from the factory JSON config and trace a single click through a 300 ms double-click window plus event-queue, debounce and wake overhead, citing code addresses in the dump. Disassembly uses an included TC32 disassembler built from a third-party opcode table; the TS0046 application image is reported byte-identical to the TS0044 one apart from factory data.

Replacement firmware v00.14 sends short presses on release and holds after 1 s, identifies as the stock TS0044/TS0046 to Zigbee2MQTT and keeps a BLE service mode for OTA. The progress table records hardware checks for earlier versions; v00.14 was flashed to a TS0046, but pairing, actions and battery reporting in Zigbee2MQTT are marked unverified. The separate ZG-226Z alarm firmware is documented as built but not yet run on hardware. This review ran nothing.

The repository has no top-level license. Firmware directories carry a permissive notice for build files taken from pvvx/BZdevice and the Telink SDK’s Apache-2.0 license, and the notes credit pvvx’s SWire work. The README calls the project highly vibe-coded; the author’s post credits a pi agent running GLM-5.3, while the reviewed files name no model and establish no REA connection.

name: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days: native PC port built on a matching decompilation
description_en: Compiles the C of the khdays-decomp matching decompilation for Windows x64 and supplies a native platform layer for the Nintendo DS hardware, SDK services and sound driver. README reports the whole game running without an ARM interpreter; its rendering, controls, mod support and network multiplayer are the port’s own additions. This is a decompilation-based port, distinct from the byte-matching DS reconstruction it builds on.
description_zh: 将 khdays-decomp 一致性反编译的 C 代码编译为 Windows x64 程序，并以原生平台层替代 Nintendo DS 硬件、SDK 服务及声音驱动。README 报告整款游戏无需 ARM 解释器即可运行；渲染、操作、模组支持与网络联机均为移植自身新增。这是基于反编译的移植，与其所依托的逐字节一致 DS 重建并非同一产物。
requirements: Reviewed version 0.1.2 is labelled work in progress. README reports the title, Story Mode, Mission Mode, combat, the shop and save round-trips running natively; builds exist only for Windows x64, with Linux, macOS, Windows on ARM and Switch listed as planned. The pinned khdays-decomp submodule (a2b0478) reports all 306 EU YKGP modules byte-identical; the port compiles that C after build-time rewriting and does not reproduce the DS binary.

Supply your own European Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days ROM (game code YKGP); the tools check it against a single supported-ROM entry before preparing local game data. Optional HD screens, videos and menus are generated from the player’s own KINGDOM HEARTS HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX and HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue copies. The repository includes no ROM, assets, SDK files or game binaries.

Building needs Windows, Visual Studio 2026 with the C++ workload, CMake, Ninja, Python 3.11+ and pycparser; running needs a Direct3D 12 or Vulkan GPU. Build preparation rewrites game pointers as DS-address references and repairs ARM calling-convention gaps from a ROM-derived Ghidra ABI table; cases it cannot repair mechanically stop at named KHDAYS_ABI_GAP points.

Reported checks are ctest suites (MSVC static analysis, short libFuzzer runs, GPU renders compared with the port’s software DS engines, a DeSmuME savestate comparison) and scripted regression walks through Mission Mode, Story Mode, saving and multiplayer. Tests needing player data are skipped without it, and CI builds only the format library on Windows and Linux. Internet play is reported tried through the maintainer’s server, local-network play between two PCs not yet; this collection ran none of these checks.

The port declares MIT; its third-party notices record the decompilation as CC0 1.0 and list SDL3 (zlib), Lua, Dear ImGui and other components under their own terms. No repository license applies to the original game or material extracted from it. README states that AI-assisted coding tools were used; no REA connection is established.

name: ico-pc: a native ICO port compiled from the PS2 decompilation
description_en: Compiles the decompiled C of the PlayStation 2 game ICO natively for Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone and Apple-silicon Macs, with host code standing in for the PS2 hardware and Sony libraries. No PS2 code is interpreted or recompiled, and the program reads the player's PAL disc image on first start. It is a native port of a separately byte-matched decompilation, with documented divergences and optional enhancements.
description_zh: 将 PlayStation 2 游戏《ICO》的反编译 C 源码原生编译到 Windows、Linux、Android、iPhone 及 Apple 芯片 Mac 上，并以宿主代码替代 PS2 硬件和 Sony 函数库。项目不解释执行或重编译任何 PS2 代码，程序在首次启动时读取玩家自备的 PAL 光盘镜像。它是另一个逐字节匹配的反编译项目的原生移植，记录了与原版的差异，并提供可选增强功能。
requirements: README describes a port of the PAL PS2 release (SCES-50760). The architecture guide says the game's decompiled C under ico2/ is compiled for the host, while port/ replaces the EE kernel, GS/VU1 rendering, SPU2 audio, disc, pad and memory-card services. Its platform table, current at release v0.7.10, lists 64-bit Windows 10/11, x86-64 and arm64 Linux, Steam Deck, Android 10+, iPhone through LiveContainer and Apple-silicon macOS 12+; the maintainer reports not testing the iPhone and Mac builds.

Requires the player's own PAL ICO disc image (SCES-50760) as .iso, .chd or .bin/.cue; other regions and editions are unsupported. Building needs no disc image, but the first run copies the game's files, about 1 GB, into the ico.o2r archive and loads the data tables from it. The legal notes exclude disc data, boot ELFs, assets and data tables from the repository and downloads.

Builds use CMake presets with Ninja. The Linux quickstart targets Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04 with gcc 14 (gcc 13 also builds), Python 3 and a fetch script that downloads about 1.6 GB of pinned toolchains and dependencies, among them llvm-mingw, mingw-w64 gcc, SDL3, Vulkan components and DXC. Rendering uses Vulkan, Direct3D 12 on Windows, or MoltenVK on Apple platforms.

CI runs hygiene and audit checks, builds and runs ctest on x86-64 and arm64 Linux, cross-builds Windows and packages Android, iPhone and macOS; disc-dependent tests skip without the player's image. The divergence list documents known differences from the PS2 and states that no test compares a run with the PS2. The upstream decompilation separately reports byte-identical PAL and Japanese boot ELFs, with most read-only data still taken from the disc; this collection did not build or run either project.

README and LICENSE apply MIT only to the project's own code, scripts and documentation, granting no rights in the game, its data or Sony and Team Ico trademarks; third-party code is listed separately. The LICENSE notice says building requires a disc image, unlike the build guide. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution.

name: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus: matching PlayStation 2 decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs source code for SCUS_971.98, the NTSC-U PlayStation 2 executable of Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus, as a work-in-progress matching decompilation. Functions not yet matched are still assembled from code split out of the user's own executable, and the build checks the linked ELF's SHA-1. The result runs in PCSX2 with the original disc for assets; it is not a native PC port.
description_zh: 将《Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus》PlayStation 2 美版可执行文件 SCUS_971.98 重建为源码，属于进行中的一致性反编译。尚未匹配的函数仍由从使用者自备可执行文件中拆分出的汇编构建，构建会检查链接后 ELF 的 SHA-1。产物需在 PCSX2 中配合原版光盘素材运行，并不是原生 PC 移植。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress decompilation of the NTSC-U executable SCUS_971.98 (SHA-1 prefix 57dc305d) that aims to decompile the game engine to matching source. Its FAQ says the project has built a matching ELF since July 2024 and still aims to match 100% of functions. Engine, Splice scripting-engine and data progress are reported on decomp.dev; this collection recorded no percentage.

The repository contains no game assets or original code. Users supply SCUS_971.98 from their own legally obtained disc, or an NTSC-U ISO for the quickstart script. Running the build requires PCSX2 2.0, the user's game ISO for assets and a BIOS from the user's own PS2.

Builds run on Debian-based Linux or WSL, with a Distrobox guide for other distributions. They need Python 3.9+ with the listed packages, MIPS binutils, Ninja, and Wine or wibo to run the downloaded ee-gcc 2.95.2 SN (ProDG) compiler archive. configure.py splits the ELF with splat, inserts split assembly in place of non-matching functions and links the executable; objdiff, decomp.me and CodeMatcher support matching, the last currently against the May 19, 2002 prototype.

By default the build checks out/SCUS_971.98 against config/checksum.sha1; --skip-checksum is documented for intentional code changes, whose output may not boot. CI downloads the original ELF through a repository secret and runs this check on main, and the check run recorded for the reviewed commit succeeded. This verifies byte identity of one executable, not complete decompilation, and this collection did not rerun it.

The repository is dedicated under CC0 1.0; the original game, extracted assembly and data, and the ProDG compiler and SCE runtime library keep separate rights. CONTRIBUTING takes mangled function names from the May 2002 prototype's debug symbols. Reviewed sources establish no REA involvement, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Pokémon Emerald: a matching Game Boy Advance decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs Pokémon Emerald for the Game Boy Advance as buildable C source, with game scripts and data kept as assembler directives. The default agbcc build produces pokeemerald.gba, and make compare checks it against the SHA-1 of the original English ROM; an optional modern-GCC build is not hash-checked. Graphics and audio sources are committed in the tree, so the documented build reads no base ROM.
description_zh: 为 Game Boy Advance 版《宝可梦 绿宝石》重建可构建的 C 源码，游戏脚本和数据以汇编指令形式保存。默认的 agbcc 构建生成 pokeemerald.gba，make compare 将其与英文原版 ROM 的 SHA-1 比对；可选的现代 GCC 构建不做哈希校验。图像和音频源文件已提交在仓库中，因此文档所述的构建流程不读取原 ROM。
requirements: README describes a decompilation of Pokémon Emerald that builds a single ROM, pokeemerald.gba; the Makefile sets game code BPEE, revision 0, and CI builds the English version. Most game code is C, while startup code, part of the m4a sound library and the GameCube multiboot library remain assembly files, and three multiboot programs (berry fix, Colosseum, e-Reader) are included as prebuilt .gba binaries. The output is a GBA ROM, not a native PC port.

The documented build reads no original ROM: graphics, audio samples and map data are committed as PNG, WAV/AIF and JSON files and converted by bundled tools. rom.sha1 records the target English release as SHA-1 f3ae088181bf583e55daf962a92bb46f4f1d07b7, and README links that ROM’s No-Intro record.

INSTALL.md covers Windows (WSL1 recommended; msys2 or Cygwin), macOS and Linux. On Debian/Ubuntu it lists build-essential, binutils-arm-none-eabi, git and libpng-dev; the matching build also needs pret/agbcc built and installed into the tree. make modern instead uses devkitARM’s arm-none-eabi-gcc and writes pokeemerald_modern.gba.

make compare runs a SHA-1 check of the built ROM against rom.sha1 and reports pokeemerald.gba: OK on a match; the Makefile notes that comparison only makes sense for non-modern builds. CI builds with COMPARE=1 and also builds the modern target. These checks establish byte identity for this one release, not gameplay coverage; this collection did not build the ROM.

The repository has no top-level license file and GitHub detects none; license files cover only some bundled tools, and agbcc’s GCC sources carry GPL v2. The original game’s code, graphics and audio remain subject to their rights holders. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Paper Mario: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation for four releases
description_en: Reconstructs Paper Mario’s Nintendo 64 code as C source that rebuilds the US, Japanese, PAL and iQue ROMs. The build takes assets and comparison inputs from a user-supplied original ROM, then checks each output against a recorded SHA-1. Mutable project reports list no remaining nonmatching functions, while the README still calls the decompilation work in progress; it is distinct from the PaperBoat native port.
description_zh: 将 Paper Mario 的 Nintendo 64 代码重建为 C 源码，可重新构建美版、日版、PAL 版和 iQue 版 ROM。构建流程从使用者自备的原 ROM 取得素材和比较输入，再将每个产物与记录的 SHA-1 比对。项目可变的进度报告显示已无未匹配函数，但 README 仍称反编译在进行中；该项目与 PaperBoat 原生移植不同。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress decompilation that builds US, JP, PAL and iQue ROMs, each with a listed SHA-1. For the reviewed commit, papermar.io’s mutable progress CSVs list zero nonmatching functions for all four versions (12,679 for US), and its US page announces 100% for US, PAL and iQue. The output is an N64 ROM, not a native PC executable; HarbourMasters’ PaperBoat port is a separate project.

At least one independently obtained original ROM matching a listed SHA-1 is required, supplied as that version’s baserom.z64; the Nix route expects all four. configure splits assets from those ROMs, and neither ROMs nor extracted assets are distributed with the source.

SETUP.md supports Linux, macOS, WSL 2 and Nix. The build uses a Python configure script with ninja, pigment64 from cargo, host MIPS binutils/GCC/cpp, and downloaded compiler builds: project GCC/binutils, GCC 2.7.2, EGCS and statically recompiled IDO 5.3. configure refuses a matching iQue build on macOS because EGCS is unavailable there.

A matching build ends with sha1sum checks against each version’s checksum.sha1, reporting “papermario.z64: OK”. --non-matching, --modern-gcc and --shift builds skip that check, so they are not matching results. Jenkins builds all four versions plus a shiftable US build and publishes the progress reports; this collection ran none of these checks.

The reviewed tree has no top-level license file and GitHub detects none, so no reuse grant is established for the source. Original ROMs and extracted assets retain separate rights, and downloaded compilers carry their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Budokai Tenkaichi 3: a native PC port built on a matching decompilation
description_en: Compiles the decompiled code of Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 (PS2, USA release SLUS-21678) for PC on a new renderer, sound, input and platform layer rather than an emulator. The game code comes from the separate BT3-Decompiled matching decompilation, and the game's data is read from the user's own disc image. The README reports the full game loop and experimental online play and says AI helped make the project; these results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 将 Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3（PS2 美版 SLUS-21678）的反编译代码编译到 PC，运行在新的渲染、音频、输入和平台层上，而非借助模拟器。游戏代码来自独立的 BT3-Decompiled 一致性反编译项目，游戏数据从使用者自备的光盘镜像读取。README 报告完整游戏流程可运行、联网对战处于实验阶段，并称项目借助 AI 完成；这些结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: README describes a native PC port of the PS2 USA release, not an emulator: the game's code from BT3-Decompiled sits in src/ and include/ with PC changes behind #ifdef PORT, on a new platform layer with Vulkan and OpenGL 3.3 renderers, sound and input. It reports the whole game loop working (boot, movies, menus, saves, fights, split screen), plus experimental online play with rollback through a Cloudflare Worker matchmaking service whose source is included; the 32-bit Linux build has no rollback. The port log in docs/port records what is and is not verified.

Supply your own disc image of the unmodified USA release (SLUS-21678) as an .iso. The setup and install.py read the game's data from it and check SHA-1 digests of the extracted main program (SLUS_216.78) and menu program (BIN/DBZP.BIN); a patched or damaged image is rejected. The repository carries the built-in data tables as shapes without values (port/data), which the program fills from the disc at start; no game data is distributed.

Releases target 64-bit x86 Linux (glibc 2.35 or newer) and Windows 10/11 with Vulkan, falling back to OpenGL; Apple Silicon macOS is experimental and source-only. On Linux, install.py checks gcc/g++, clang with its Python bindings for the 64-bit pointer rewriting, glslc and SDL3, then reads the disc, builds the program and runs the game's demo fight headless as a self-test. Linux and Windows release archives are built in a Docker container (clang/LLVM, SDL3, mingw-w64) without any disc input.

The BT3-Decompiled README reports 99.92% of the main program's game code and 99.97% of the menu program in matching C, with both rebuilt binaries byte-identical; Sony SDK and CRI libraries are out of scope. The port log reports a replay recorded in PCSX2 matching console health values at sampled ticks and the final clock, while an early entry still noted differing fighter state words; macOS is reported to match the Linux state on every demo frame. These remain project-reported, and this collection ran nothing.

The port's own code is AGPL-3.0-only after commit 06e4671 and MIT up to and including it; bundled libraries keep their own terms. README states that the game code in src/ and include/ belongs to the game's rights holders, and BT3-Decompiled's CC0 1.0 dedication covers only its own reconstruction work. README says the project was made with AI help, and the docs carry working rules for parallel decompilation agents; no REA use is documented and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: GoonFi V2: byte-identical Rust recompilation of a Solana program
description_en: OtterSec researchers describe an agent pipeline that reconstructed Rust source for the closed-source GoonFi V2 Solana program until a rebuild with the original toolchain reproduced the deployed ELF. Per-function instruction scoring, a deterministic merge judge and bans on assembly and other score-gaming constructs steered the agents; matching function order and panic-location paths closed the last differences. The article and a companion repository document the method and a verification script, while the internal tooling and agent transcripts remain unpublished.
description_zh: OtterSec 研究人员介绍了一套智能体流程：为闭源的 GoonFi V2 Solana 程序重建 Rust 源码，直至用原工具链重新构建即可复现所部署的 ELF。逐函数指令评分、确定性合并评审，以及对汇编等刷分写法的禁用约束引导智能体工作；对齐函数顺序和 panic 位置路径后，最后的差异得以消除。文章与配套仓库记录了方法和验证脚本，内部工具及智能体对话记录仍未公开。
requirements: The article by Renato Marziano and Robert Chen is dated 2026-10-15. Its target is the GoonFi V2 sBPF program as originally deployed at slot 448984043, which the verification script identifies as a 243,080-byte ELF; the article shows 26,432 .text instructions. The companion README says the live program was upgraded on 2026-10-06 to fix the reported bugs, so current on-chain code is a different build. The output is reconstructed Rust source, not a client for the protocol or an update of the live program.

The described inputs are the deployed binary, the program’s IDL and on-chain transactions. The authors report using Claude Opus 5.5 as orchestrator with Astra subagents, an architect agent that split work by top-level instruction, per-worker branches, Binary Ninja with their bn-ebpf-solana plugin, their earlier patina-research setup, an ibrl.golf diff viewer forked from decomp.me, and on-chain data services. They call the core pipeline internal tooling; its harness, judge and agent transcripts are not published.

Each function is scored by aligning its instructions with the target: 100 points per missing or extra instruction, 60 per misordered one, 5 per wrong register or immediate and 1 per stack-offset byte. A deterministic judge rebuilt the program on every commit and merged only total-score gains with no function regressing and no flagged construct; an LLVM pass plugin banned score-gaming constructs, and patterns such as asm!, black_box, volatile writes, transmute and exported internal helpers were banned or penalized. Reviewer and orchestrator agents handled readability. Per-function matches still left a diff of about 93k bytes, closed by matching function order and panic-location file paths and line numbers.

The repository’s build.sh downloads Solana platform-tools v1.48 for Linux x86-64 (rustc 1.84.1-dev, LLVM 19.1.7), runs a locked cargo build, strips the result and prints its SHA-256; the expected value is 6a2a8670…600f767d. VERIFY.sh also needs an Alchemy archive key or another archival RPC, because the original ELF survives only in the deploy transaction’s buffer writes, and compares the reassembled ELF with the build byte for byte. No binary is committed. The README describes the check as a match beyond padding, while the script compares exactly; this collection ran neither.

The article reports that an auditing agent then found a critical accounting vulnerability and says it was responsibly disclosed; exploitation details are out of scope here. The companion repository declares no license, and its source is reconstructed from a third party’s closed-source program, so reuse rights are unclear and remain with the program’s owners. The reviewed sources establish no REA use, and agent results remain author-reported.
